page_data.en:
Special Branch.
October 9, 1935.

Activities of the Shanghai Telegraph Office of the
Ministry of Communications regarding suspected
installation of a wireless transmitting set at 119
Baikal Road.

In July this year, a report was received in this Branch
to the effect that an unauthorised radio transmitting set was
being operated in the Eastern District. Enquiries were
instituted by the foreign and Chinese members of the staff of
S.I., and, although no definite evidence could be obtained,
suspicions were aroused concerning house No.119 Baikal Road,
the residence of a foreign employee of the S.M.C., C.A. McLellan.
This man, a British subject, is an inspector in the P.W.D., and
suspicions were aroused partly from the fact that the aerial
equipment above the house seemed to be beyond the requirements of
the most powerful receiving set. Two fairly large masts are
erected outside the house, and the antenna is equipped with
approximately 40 insulators. This apparatus has given rise to
considerable discussion among the foreign residents of Wayside
district, but no one has succeeded in obtaining an invitation
to examine the radio inside the house. Only one or two of
Mr. and Mrs. McLellan's most intimate associates are allowed
to enter the house, and all business is conducted on the doorstep.

Mr. McLellan is on intimate terms with Landesen, a well-
known Soviet agent and has introduced him to a Masonic lodge.
Mrs. McLellan is of Russian extraction, and has three brothers
who are Soviet employees in Vladivostock; one of them is a
member of the G.P.U. She has visited Vladivostock two or three
times during the last few years. She openly states that she is
pro-Soviet. Until recently two other persons were residing in
page_data.zh:
特别支部。
1935年10月9日。

交通部上海电报局关于涉嫌在贝加尔路119号安装无线发射装置的活动情况。

今年7月，本支部收到报告称，东区有人操作未经授权的无线电发射装置。工部局警务处（S.I.）的外籍和华籍职员进行了查询，虽然未能获得确凿证据，但对贝加尔路119号产生了怀疑，该处是工部局外籍雇员 C.A. 麦克莱伦的住所。此人系英国臣民，是工务处（P.W.D.）的一名督察。引起怀疑的部分原因是，该房屋上方的天线设备似乎超出了最强力接收机的需求。屋外竖立着两根相当高的桅杆，天线上装有约40个绝缘子。这套装置在韦赛德（Wayside）地区的外侨中引起了诸多议论，但无人成功获邀进屋检查内部的无线电设备。只有麦克莱伦夫妇最亲密的一两个associates被允许进入屋内，所有事务均在门口处理。

麦克莱伦与著名的苏联特工兰迪森（Landesen）关系密切，并曾将其引荐入共济会分会。麦克莱伦夫人具有俄罗斯血统，她在符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）有三个兄弟，均为苏联雇员；其中一人是格别乌（G.P.U.）成员。在过去几年中，她曾两三次访问符拉迪沃斯托克。她公开表示自己是亲苏派的。直到最近，还有另外两人居住在

page_data.en:
-2-
the house with the McLellans, one a Filipino and the other an
attractive looking young foreign woman said to be the wife or
paramour of the Filipino. Apart from the fact that she was
the constant companion of Mrs. McLellan, nothing is known of
this woman.
Enquiries regarding the Filipino are still in progress.
It is known that he has been in communication with a student or
students of the Futan University. During the past few months
he has made several trips abroad, and always returned with large
sums of money. There is every reason to believe that his name
is Ramon Caro, an American subject, erstwhile owner of the Ram
Car Company in Manila, and having a doubtful reputation. He is
the associate of a British Eurasian named T.K. Knight, the owner
of the Oxidite Battery Corp., lane 156, T.55-57, Liaoyang Road.
Knight has accompanied Caro on his journeys abroad. Both Knight
and Caro have a thorough knowledge of radio.
Efforts to keep a watch on the movements of Mr. McLellan
have not proved successful, owing to the fact that he is ever on
his guard and carefully avoids answering personal questions, and
also because he has a fast car and it is practically impossible
to follow him. There is reason to believe that he visited the
Soviet ship s.s. "Sever" when she was in Shanghai on Saturday,
August 17.
On October 4, a search warrant was forwarded to the
Special Branch issued by the Shanghai Special District Court at
the request of the Shanghai Telegraph Administration Office to
search and seize an unauthorised radio transmitting set at 119
Baikal Road. An inspector of the Administration Office who
attended was informed that this was the residence of a British
subject and the warrant could not be executed, and was referred
to the British Court. When questioned regarding his grounds
page_data.zh:
-2-
麦克莱伦夫妇的家中，一人是菲律宾人，另一人是外貌迷人的年轻外籍女子，据称是这名菲律宾人的妻子或情妇。除了她是麦克莱伦夫人的常伴之外，对该女子一无所知。
对这名菲律宾人的调查仍在进行中。已知他与复旦大学的一名或多名学生有联系。在过去几个月里，他数次出国旅行，且每次回来都携带大量现金。有充分理由相信，他的名字是拉蒙·卡罗（Ramon Caro），美国臣民，曾是马尼拉 Ram Car 公司的所有者，声誉不佳。他与一名名叫 T.K. 奈特（T.K. Knight）的英籍欧亚混血儿有交往，奈特是辽阳路 T.55-57 弄156号氧化电池公司（Oxidite Battery Corp.）的所有者。奈特曾陪同卡罗出国旅行。奈特和卡罗都精通无线电知识。
由于麦克莱伦先生时刻警惕，谨慎避免回答个人问题，加之他拥有一辆快车，实际上无法跟踪，因此监视其行踪的努力并未成功。有理由相信，他在8月17日星期六苏联轮船“谢韦尔”号（s.s. "Sever"）停靠上海期间曾登船访问。
10月4日，应上海电政管理局的请求，上海特区地方法院向特别支部签发了一份搜查令，旨在搜查并扣押贝加尔路119号未经授权的无线电发射装置。到场执行的一名电政管理局督察被告知，此处为英国臣民的住所，该搜查令无法执行，并被指引至英国法院。当被问及他认为该地址安装有发射装置的依据时，

page_data.en:
-3-

for believing that a transmitting set was installed at that
address, the inspector stated that tests had been carried
out with radio beam direction finding instruments, and the
tests had proved that a transmitting set was installed at
119 Baikal Road.

At 10.35 p.m., October 6, Mr. McLellan telephoned
to Bayside Station and stated that a suspicious character
was loitering outside his house. Police attended and took
into custody a male Chinese who proved to be an agent of the
Shanghai Telegraph Administration who had been detailed to
collect information regarding the radio alleged to be installed
at 119 Baikal Road. This man was later released and warned
not to continue his observation duty.

Certified true copy.

....................
page_data.zh:
-3-

该督察表示，已使用无线电波束测向仪器进行了测试，测试结果证明贝加尔路119号安装有一部发射装置。

10月6日晚上10点35分，麦克莱伦先生打电话给百老汇路警察局（Bayside Station），称有一名可疑人物在他家屋外徘徊。警察赶到并拘留了一名中国男子，经查实其为上海电政管理局的特工，奉命收集有关据称安装在贝加尔路119号的无线电装置的情报。此人随后被释放，并被告诫不得继续执行观察任务。

经核证无误副本。

page_data.en:
Special Branch.
October 6th, 1935.

Cancellation of Shanghai Special District Court
Search Warrant No.8144.

Shanghai Special District Court Search Warrant,
No.8144, issued on October 4, 1935, at the instance of the
Shanghai Telegraph Office of the Ministry of Communications,
for the seizure of a wireless transmitting and receiving set
at 119 Baikal Road, is herewith forwarded for return to the
Court for cancellation.

The warrant could not be executed as the occupant
of 119 Baikal Road does not come under the jurisdiction of
the Shanghai Special District Court, being a British subject.

Certified true copy.

W. Greens
page_data.zh:
特别支部。
1935年10月6日。

撤销上海特区地方法院第8144号搜查令。

现随函退回上海特区地方法院于1935年10月4日应交通部上海电报局之请求签发的第8144号搜查令，以便法院予以撤销。该搜查令旨在扣押贝加尔路119号的无线收发装置。

该搜查令无法执行，因为贝加尔路119号的住户是英国臣民，不属于上海特区地方法院的管辖范围。

经核证无误副本。

W. 格林斯（Greens）

page_data.en:
Special Branch.
October 4, 1935.

Receipt of Shanghai Special District Court Warrant for
Seizure of Wireless Transmitting and Receiving Set at
119 Baikal Road.

At 12 noon October 4, 1935, a Search Warrant, No.8144,
issued by the Shanghai Special District Court at the instance
of the Shanghai Telegraph Office of the Ministry of Communications,
was received by the D.C. (Sp.Br.) for the seizure of a wireless
transmitting and receiving set at 119 Baikal Road.

Before executing this Warrant, inquiries were made
regarding the nationality of the occupant of 119 Baikal Road,
and it was found that the tenant is a British subject. He is
C.A. McClellan employed as inspector in the P.W.D. of the Council.

Hsu Tsong-nien (許宗毅), acting on behalf of the
Shanghai Telegraph Office, has been informed of the nationality
of the occupant of 119 Baikal Road, and that a Shanghai Special
District Court Warrant cannot be executed in this case. He has
asked what action the Municipal Police can now take in the case.

The representative when questioned about the source of
the information regarding the location of the transmitting set
stated that it had been traced by the Government Radio
Administration by means of "detectors" or "finders".

Certified true copy.

....................
page_data.zh:
特别支部。
1935年10月4日。

收到上海特区地方法院关于扣押贝加尔路119号无线收发装置的搜查令。

1935年10月4日中午12时，特别支部副主任（D.C. (Sp.Br.)）收到了上海特区地方法院应交通部上海电报局之请求签发的第8144号搜查令，旨在扣押贝加尔路119号的无线收发装置。

在执行此搜查令之前，对贝加尔路119号住户的国籍进行了查询，发现租户为英国臣民。他是 C.A. 麦克莱伦（C.A. McClellan），受雇于工部局工务处（P.W.D.）担任督察。

代表上海电报局行事的许宗毅（Hsu Tsong-nien）已获悉贝加尔路119号住户的国籍，以及上海特区地方法院的搜查令在此案中无法执行的情况。他询问市政警察在此案中现在可以采取何种行动。

当被问及关于发射装置位置的信息来源时，该代表表示，这是由政府无线电管理处通过“探测器”或“ finder ”追踪到的。

经核证无误副本。

在此事件发生后不久，麦克莱伦先生解雇了他的两名仆人。

经核证无误副本。

Special Branch.
October 9, 1935.

Activities of the Shanghai Telegraph Office of the
Ministry of Communications regarding suspected
installation of a wireless transmitting set at 119
Baikal Road.

In July this year, a report was received in this Branch
to the effect that an unauthorised radio transmitting set was
being operated in the Eastern District. Enquiries were
instituted by the foreign and Chinese members of the staff of
S.I., and, although no definite evidence could be obtained,
suspicions were aroused concerning house No.119 Baikal Road,
the residence of a foreign employee of the S.M.C., C.A. McLellan.
This man, a British subject, is an inspector in the P.W.D., and
suspicions were aroused partly from the fact that the aerial
equipment above the house seemed to be beyond the requirements of
the most powerful receiving set. Two fairly large masts are
erected outside the house, and the antenna is equipped with
approximately 40 insulators. This apparatus has given rise to
considerable discussion among the foreign residents of Wayside
district, but no one has succeeded in obtaining an invitation
to examine the radio inside the house. Only one or two of
Mr. and Mrs. McLellan's most intimate associates are allowed
to enter the house, and all business is conducted on the doorstep.

Mr. McLellan is on intimate terms with Landesen, a well-
known Soviet agent and has introduced him to a Masonic lodge.
Mrs. McLellan is of Russian extraction, and has three brothers
who are Soviet employees in Vladivostock; one of them is a
member of the G.P.U. She has visited Vladivostock two or three
times during the last few years. She openly states that she is
pro-Soviet. Until recently two other persons were residing in
page_data.zh:
特科。
1935年10月9日。

关于交通部上海电报局就贝加尔路119号疑似安装无线发射机一事的活动。

今年七月，本科收到一份报告，称东区有人操作未经授权的无线电发射机。工部局警务处（S.I.）的外籍和华人职员随即展开调查，虽然未能获得确凿证据，但对贝加尔路119号产生了怀疑，该处是工部局外籍雇员 C.A. McLellan 的住所。此人为英国臣民，任工务处（P.W.D.）督察，引起怀疑的部分原因是该房屋上方的天线设备似乎超出了最强力接收机的需求。屋外竖立着两根相当高的桅杆，天线上装有约40个绝缘子。这套装置在韦赛德（Wayside，音译）区的外侨中引起了诸多议论，但无人成功获邀进屋检查内部的无线电设备。只有麦克莱伦（McLellan）夫妇最亲密的一两位associates被允许进入屋内，所有事务均在门口进行。

麦克莱伦先生与著名的苏联代理人 Landesen（音译）关系密切，并曾将其引荐入共济会分会。麦克莱伦夫人具有俄罗斯血统，有三个兄弟在符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）担任苏联职员；其中一人是格别乌（G.P.U.）成员。在过去几年中，她曾两三次访问符拉迪沃斯托克。她公开表示自己是亲苏的。直到最近，还有另外两人居住在

page_data.en:
- 2 -

the house with the McLellans, one a Filipino and the other an
attractive looking young foreign woman said to be the wife or
paramour of the Filipino. Apart from the fact that she was
the constant companion of Mrs. McLellan, nothing is known of
this woman.

Enquiries regarding the Filipino are still in progress.
It is known that he has been in communication with a student or
students of the Futan University. During the past few months
he has made several trips abroad, and always returned with large
sums of money. There is every reason to believe that his name
is Ramon Caro, an American subject, erstwhile owner of the Ram
Car Company in Manila, and having a doubtful reputation. He is
the associate of a British Eurasian named T.K. Knight, the owner
of the Oxidite Battery Corps., lane 156, T55-67, Liaoyang Road.
Knight has accompanied Caro on his journeys abroad. Both Knight
and Caro have a thorough knowledge of radio.

Efforts to keep a watch on the movements of Mr. McLellan
have not proved successful, owing to the fact that he is ever on
his guard and carefully avoids answering personal questions, and
also because he has a fast car and it is practically impossible
to follow him. There is reason to believe that he visited the
Soviet ship s.s. "SEVER" when she was in Shanghai on Saturday,
August 17.

On October 4, a search warrant was forwarded to the
Special Branch issued by the Shanghai Special District Court at
the request of the Shanghai Telegraph Administration Office to
search and seize an unauthorised radio transmitting set at 119
Baikal Road. An inspector of the Administration Office who
attended was informed that this was the residence of a British
subject and the warrant could not be executed, and was referred
to the British Court. When questioned regarding his grounds
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

麦克莱伦夫妇的家中，一人为菲律宾人，另一人为外貌迷人的年轻外籍女性，据称是这名菲律宾人的妻子或情妇。除了她是麦克莱伦夫人的常伴之外，对此女一无所知。

针对该菲律宾人的调查仍在进行中。已知他与复旦大学的一名或多名学生有联系。在过去几个月里，他多次出国旅行，且每次回来都携带大量现金。有充分理由相信他的名字是 Ramon Caro（音译），美国公民，曾是马尼拉 Ram Car Company（音译）的所有者，声誉不佳。他与一名名为 T.K. Knight（音译）的英籍欧亚混血儿有关联，后者是辽阳路 T55-67号 156弄 Oxidite Battery Corps.（音译）的所有者。Knight 曾陪同 Caro 出国旅行。Knight 和 Caro 均精通无线电知识。

由于麦克莱伦先生时刻警惕，谨慎避免回答个人问题，加之他拥有一辆快车，实际上无法跟踪，因此监视其行踪的努力并未成功。有理由相信，他在8月17日星期六苏联轮船“SEVER”号（注：下文亦作“SEMEN”号）停靠上海期间曾登船拜访。

10月4日，应上海电报管理局的请求，上海特区地方法院向特科签发了一份搜查令，旨在搜查并扣押贝加尔路119号未经授权的无线电发射机。到场的一名管理局督察被告知，此处为英国臣民的住所，搜查令无法执行，并被指引至英国法院。当被问及认为该地址安装有发射机的依据时，

At 10.35 p.m. October 6, Mr. McLellan telephoned
to Wayside Station and stated that a suspicious character
was loitering outside his house. Police attended and took
into custody a male Chinese who proved to be an agent of the

Special Branch.
October 4, 1935.

Receipt of Shanghai Special District Court Warrant for
Seizure of Wireless Transmitting and Receiving Set at
119 Baikal Road.

At 12 noon October 4, 1935, a Search warrant, No.8144,
issued by the Shanghai Special District Court at the instance
of the Shanghai Telegraph Office of the Ministry of Communications,
was received by the D.C. (Sp.Br.) for the seizure of a wireless
transmitting and receiving set at 119 Baikal Road.

Before executing this warrant, inquiries were made
regarding the nationality of the occupant of 119 Baikal Road,
and it was found that the tenant is a British subject. He is
C.A. McLellan employed as inspector in the P.W.D. of the Council.

Hsu Tsong-nien (許宗毅), acting on behalf of the
Shanghai Telegraph Office, has been informed of the nationality
of the occupant of 119 Baikal Road, and that a Shanghai Special
District Court Warrant cannot be executed in this case. He has
asked what action the Municipal Police can now take in the case.

The representative when questioned about the source of
the information regarding the location of the transmitting set
stated that it had been traced by the Government Radio
Administration by means of "detectors" or "finders".

Certified true copy.

1935年10月4日。

收到上海特区地方法院关于扣押贝加尔路119号无线收发机的搜查令。

1935年10月4日中午12时，特科副主管（D.C. (Sp.Br.)）收到了上海特区地方法院应交通部上海电报局之请签发的第8144号搜查令，旨在扣押贝加尔路119号的无线收发机。

在执行此搜查令之前，对贝加尔路119号居住者的国籍进行了查询，发现租户为英国臣民。他是 C.A. McLellan，受雇于工部局工务处（P.W.D.）担任督察。

代表上海电报局行事的许宗毅（Hsu Tsong-nien）已获悉贝加尔路119号居住者的国籍，以及上海特区地方法院的搜查令在此案中无法执行。他询问市政警察在此案中现在可以采取何种行动。

当被问及关于发射机位置信息的来源时，该代表表示，这是政府无线电管理处通过“探测器”或“ finder ”追踪到的。

核证无误副本。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
October 21st, 1935.
S. L. REGISTRY
S. B. D. 6818
22 10 35

Dear Bourne,

The Consul-General has received a letter from the
Telegraph Administration alleging that a British
subject named McLellan residing at 119, Baikal Road is
operating a wireless transmitting set. Translation of
the letter is enclosed herewith.

It is true that there are no regulations binding
on British subjects to prevent the use of such sets
but under a resolution passed at the Washington
Conference the establishment of radio stations in China
by foreigners is restricted and we have always dis-
couraged the setting up of any station by British
subjects without the consent of the Chinese authorities.

The Consul-General would be much obliged if the
Shanghai Municipal Police could supply him with any
information regarding McLellan and his wireless
activities.

Yours sincerely,
J. G. O. Davidson

Major K.M. Bourne, M.C.,
Acting Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

亲爱的 Bourne：

总领事收到电报管理局的一封信，指控居住在贝加尔路119号的英国臣民 McLellan 正在操作无线发射机。随函附上该信的译文。

确实，没有约束英国臣民禁止使用此类设备的法规，但根据华盛顿会议通过的一项决议，外国人在中国建立电台受到限制，且我们一直不鼓励英国臣民在未获得中国政府同意的情况下设立任何电台。

如上海公共租界工部局警务处能提供有关 McLellan 及其无线电活动的任何信息，总领事将不胜感激。

From the Ministry of Communications Telegraph Adminis-
tration, Shanghai, to H.B.M. Consul-General, Shanghai.
October 4th, 1935.

Sir,

This Administration has recently received a secret report
to the following effect:

"In the house at No.119, Baikal Road, Shanghai, there is a
privately established wireless station which transmits and
receives messages in contravention of the law."

The Shanghai First Special District Court was immediately
requested to investigate and take action in accordance with law.
It has now been discovered that the occupier of the above house
is a British subject, and action should be taken with the
assistance of the British Consulate. The establishment of a
private wireless station is strictly prohibited by the laws and
orders of China, and should be punished by law.

I am now sending Mr. Hsu Tsung-J, an official of this
Administration, to call on you with this letter, and explain
everything to you verbally. I shall be very grateful if you will
give approval to sending an official in the company of Mr. Hsu
to go to the above address and make a search, in order to help
the administration of telegraph matters.

I have long been aware that your country has always respect-
ed the authority of the law, and, moreover, that a guiding
principle with you is the sincere cultivation of friendly inter-
national relations, and therefore your assistance will of course
/be

阁下：

本局近期收到一份秘密报告，内容如下：

“在上海贝加尔路119号房屋内，设有一私建无线电台，违法收发报文。”

当即请求上海第一特区地方法院依法调查并采取行动。现已查明，上述房屋的居住者为英国臣民，应在英国领事馆的协助下采取行动。中国法令严禁私设无线电台，违者应依法惩处。

现派本局官员许宗毅（Hsu Tsung-J，音译）携此函拜会阁下，并向阁下口头说明一切。如蒙批准派员陪同许先生前往上述地址进行搜查，以协助电政管理，本人将不胜感激。

本人久知贵国一向尊重法律权威，且以真诚培养国际友好关系为指导原则，因此贵方自当给予协助。

Subject (in full) Suspected installation of a radio set at 119 Baikal Road

In connection with the suspected installation of an
unauthorised transmitting set at 119 Baikal Road, I have to report
that Mr. C. A. McLellan, the occupant of the premises and an
employee of the S.M.C., during a conversation with an acquaintance
admitted that he had a combined transmitting and receiving set
installed in his house, and that this set was specially imported
from America for him by the directors of Radio Station XMHA. He
added that though he had never used the set for transmitting
purposes, he had frequently loaned it to Radio Station XMHA.
Radio Station XMHA is sponsored by the Radio Engineering
Co., 445 Racecourse Road. Dr. W.H. Downs, an American dental
surgeon, is said to possess the major financial interest in the
venture.
Regarding the incident on October 6, when an agent of
the Shanghai Telegraph Administration was arrested at the request
of Mr. McLellan for loitering outside his house, but later
released, Mr. McLellan mentioned that he had reported the matter
to the British Consulate-General.
Mr. McLellan dismissed his two servants shortly after
this incident.
D. S.

Station,
REPORT
Date October 9, 1935

Subject Activities of the Shanghai Telegraph Office of the Ministry
of Communications regarding suspected installation of a wireless
transmitting set at 119 Baikal Road.
Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by A. Gault (Sig)

In July this year, a report was received in this
Branch to the effect that an unauthorised radio transmitting
set was being operated in the Eastern District. Enquiries
were instituted by the foreign and Chinese members of the
staff of S.l., and, although no definite evidence could be
obtained, suspicions were aroused concerning house No.119
Baikal Road, the residence of a foreign employee of the
S.M.C., C.A.McLellan. This man, a British subject, is an
inspector in the P.W.D., and suspicions were aroused partly
from the fact that the aerial equipment above the house
seemed to be beyond the requirements of the most powerful
receiving set. Two fairly large masts are erected outside
the house, and the antenna is equipped with approximately
40 insulators. This apparatus has given rise to considerable
discussion among the foreign residents of Wayside district,
but no one has succeeded in obtaining an invitation to
examine the radio inside the house. Only one or two of
Mr. and Mrs. McLellan's most intimate associates are
allowed to enter the house, and all business is conducted
on the doorstep.

* See So.8010
Mr. McLellan is on intimate terms with Landesén, a
well-known Soviet agent and has introduced him to a Masonic
lodge. Mrs. McLellan is of Russian extraction, and has
three brothers who are Soviet employees in Vladivostock;
one of them is a member of the G.P.U. She has visited
Vladivostock two or three times during the last few years.
She openly states that she is pro-Soviet. Until recently
two other persons were residing in the house with the
McLellans, one a Filipino and the other an attractive

主题 关于交通部上海电报局涉嫌在贝加尔路119号安装无线发射装置的活动的报告。
由 D.S. McKeown 制作 由 A. Gault (签名) 转呈

今年七月，本科收到一份报告，称东区有人操作未经授权的无线电发射装置。S.l. 的外籍和华人职员开展了调查，虽然未能获得确凿证据，但对贝加尔路119号产生了怀疑，该处是工部局外籍雇员 C.A.McLellan 的住所。此人为英国臣民，是工务处的督察，引起怀疑的部分原因是，该房屋上方的天线设备似乎超出了最强力接收机的需求。屋外竖立着两根相当高的桅杆，天线上装有约40个绝缘子。这套设备在韦赛德区的外国居民中引起了广泛讨论，但没有人成功获邀进入屋内检查无线电设备。只有麦克莱伦夫妇的一两个最亲密的伙伴才被允许进入屋内，所有事务均在门口进行。

* 参见 So.8010
麦克莱伦先生与著名的苏联特工 Landesén 关系密切，并已将后者引入一个共济会分会。麦克莱伦夫人具有俄罗斯血统，她在符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）有三个兄弟，均为苏联雇员；其中一人是格别乌（G.P.U.）成员。在过去几年里，她曾两三次访问符拉迪沃斯托克。她公开声称自己亲苏。直到最近，还有另外两人住在麦克莱伦家中，一人是菲律宾人，另一人是

looking young foreign woman said to be the wife or paramour
of the Filipino. Apart from the fact that she was the
constant companion of Mrs. McLellan, nothing is known of
this woman.
        Enquiries regarding the Filipino are still in progress.
It is known that he has been in communication with a student
or students of the Futan University. During the past few
months he has made several trips abroad, and always returned
with large sums of money. There is every reason to believe
that his name is Ramon Caro, an American subject, erstwhile
owner of the Ram Car Company in Manila, and having a doubtful
reputation. He is the associate of a British Eurasian named
T.K.Knight, the owner of the Oxidite Battery Corp., lane 156,
T.55-57, Liaoyang Road. Knight has accompanied Caro on
his journeys abroad. Both Knight and Caro have a thorough
knowledge of radio.
        Efforts to keep a watch on the movements of Mr.
McLellan have not proved successful, owing to the fact that
he is ever on his guard and carefully avoids answering
personal questions, and also because he has a fast car
and it is practically impossible to follow him. There is
reason to believe that he visited the Soviet ship s.s.
"Sever" when she was in Shanghai on Saturday, Aug. 17.
        On October 4, a search warrant was forwarded to the
Special Branch issued by the Shanghai Special District
Court at the request of the Shanghai Telegraph Administration
Office to search and seize an unauthorised radio transmitting
set at 119 Baikal Road. An inspector of the Administration
Office who attended was informed that this was the residence

        关于该菲律宾人的调查仍在进行中。已知他与复旦大学的某位或某些学生有联系。在过去几个月里，他多次出国旅行，且总是带着大笔钱款回来。我们有充分理由相信，他的名字是 Ramon Caro，美国臣民，曾是马尼拉 Ram Car 公司的老板，声誉不佳。他是名为 T.K.Knight 的英籍欧亚混血儿的伙伴，后者是氧化电池公司（Oxidite Battery Corp.）的所有者，地址为辽阳路 T.55-57号，156弄。Knight 曾陪同 Caro 出国旅行。Knight 和 Caro 都精通无线电知识。
        由于麦克莱伦先生时刻保持警惕，小心翼翼地避免回答个人问题，加之他拥有一辆快车，实际上无法跟踪，因此监视其行踪的努力并未成功。有理由相信，他在8月17日星期六苏联轮船“Sever”号停靠上海期间曾登船访问。
        10月4日，应上海电报管理局的请求，上海特区地方法院向特科签发了一份搜查令，以搜查并扣押贝加尔路119号未经授权的无线电发射装置。到场的一位电报管理局督察被告知，这是

Date 6th October 19 35.
Subject Activities of a member of The Chinese Telegram Administration,
Shanghai.
Made by D.S.MacLennan. Forwarded by
Sir,
At 10.35 p.m. 6-10-35 a telephone message was received
from Mr. C.A.Maclellan, attached to the S.M.C. Public Works
Department and residing at No. 119, Baikal Road, to the effect
that a male Chinese was loitering in the vicinity of his home.
S.I.Salt, C.D.C. 300 and the undersigned immediately
attended and, on arrival at Baikal Road, near Informant's
address, found C.P.C. 2001 with the suspect under arrest, his
description being as follows:-
Named Ta Zang Sung(朱长生 ) age 21, native of Shanghai,
m/Telegram deliverer, residing in Nantao.
Mr. Maclellan was located at his home and identified the
suspect as being the person in question, he having observed
him loitering in that vicinity both on the nights of 5 and
6-10-35.
C.P.C. 2001, when questioned, stated that he had arrested
the man on Baikal Road at the instigation of two unknown
foreigners on suspicion of loitering. Mr. Maclellan denied
that he was one of the two foreigners.
The suspect, when brought to the station, stated that for
the past year he had been employed by The Chinese Telegram
Association as a messenger boy at the Nantao office.
On 8-10-35 he was transferred to the Settlement office at
200 Szechuen Road, and detailed for Special duty on Baikal
and Macgregor roads to secretly record the houses in which
radios are installed.
The undersigned escorted the suspect to the office at 200
Szechuen Road, where the manager named Yuen Ling(袁林 )
verified his statement and gave a written chit to that effect.

主题 中华电信管理局上海分局一名成员的活动。
由 D.S.MacLennan 制作。转呈人
先生，
1935年10月6日晚上10点35分，接到隶属于工部局工务处、居住在贝加尔路119号的 C.A.Maclellan 先生的电话消息，称有一名中国男子在他家附近徘徊。
S.I.Salt, C.D.C. 300 和本人立即前往，到达报案人地址附近的贝加尔路时，发现 C.P.C. 2001 已将嫌疑人逮捕，其描述如下：-
姓名 Ta Zang Sung (朱长生)，年龄21岁，上海籍，职业/电报投递员，居住在南市。
找到在家中的 Maclellan 先生，他指认该嫌疑人即为所涉之人，他曾在1935年10月5日和6日夜间观察到该人在该区域徘徊。
C.P.C. 2001 在接受询问时表示，他是受两名不明身份的外国人指使，以涉嫌徘徊为由在贝加尔路逮捕了该男子。Maclellan 先生否认自己是那两名外国人之一。
嫌疑人被带到警局后表示，过去一年他受雇于中华电信协会，在南市办事处担任信差。
1935年10月8日，他被调往四川路200号的租界办事处，并被指派在贝加尔路和麦格雷戈路执行特殊任务，秘密记录安装无线电设备的房屋。
本人护送嫌疑人前往四川路200号的办事处，经理袁林 (Yuen Ling) 核实了他的陈述，并就此出具了书面便条。

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Grubb

At 12 noon October 4, 1935, a Search Warrant,
No. 8144, issued by the Shanghai Special District Court at
the instance of the Shanghai Telegraph Office of the Ministry
of Communications, was received by the D.C. (Sp.Br.) for the
seizure of a wireless transmitting and receiving set at 119
Baikal Road.
Before executing this Warrant, inquiries were
made regarding the nationality of the occupant of 119 Baikal
Road, and it was found that the tenant is a British subject.
He is C.A. McLellan employed as inspector in the P.W.D. of the
Council.
Hsu Tsong-nien(許宗毅), acting on behalf of the
Shanghai Telegraph Office, has been informed of the nationality
of the occupant of 119 Baikal Road, and that a S.S.D.Court
Warrant cannot be executed in this case. He has asked what
action the Municipal Police can now take in the case.
The representative when questioned about the source
of the information regarding the location of the transmitting
set stated that it had been traced by the Government Radio
Administration by means of "detectors" or "finders".

事由：收到上海特区地方法院关于搜查贝加尔路119号无线收发报机的令状。

由首席侦探格鲁布（Grubb）撰写并转呈

1935年10月4日中午12时，应交通部上海电报局之请求，由上海特区地方法院签发的第8144号搜查令送达副督察长（特别科），旨在搜查并扣押贝加尔路119号的一台无线收发报机。
在执行该令状之前，对贝加尔路119号居住者的国籍进行了查询，查明租户为英国臣民。他是C.A. McLellan，受雇于工部局工务处担任督察。
代表上海电报局行事的许宗毅（Hsu Tsong-nien）已获知贝加尔路119号居住者的国籍情况，并被告知在此情况下无法执行上海特区地方法院的令状。他询问工部局警务处目前在此案中可采取何种行动。
当被问及关于发射机位置信息的来源时，该代表称是由政府无线电管理处通过“探测器”或“查找器”追踪确定的。

With reference to the attached report on the
broadcasting of an obscene story from the Li Zu Tuh Daung
Broadcasting Station, 250 Burkill Road, on December 28,
enquiries show that the troupe concerned is managed by
Tsu Zien-kung (male) and Tsang Mei Yuin (female), and
consists of six persons (3 male and 3 female). Tsu and
Tsang who are singers of Pootung songs, obtained the contract
for broadcasting daily between 1.30 p.m. and 2.15 p.m. from
the Li Zu Tuh Daung Broadcasting Station about six months ago;
the contract expired on January 1, 1937. The programme
differed every day and consequently the story mentioned in
the attached report has not been repeated since December 28,
1936.

Tsang Mei-yuin (張美雲), one of the managers
of the troupe, during an interview, denied any knowledge of
the broadcasting of the story in question, but stated that
some of the troupe might have broadcasted the story without
permission. She gave assurance that stricter surveillance
would be exercised in future.

Singers of the Pootung songs or stories have a
society entitled the "Pootung Song Research Society"
(上海市申曲歌劇研究會) with an office at 8 Foh Chong Li,

该会在当地党部和市社会局的监督下管理，其宗旨是净化歌曲中的淫秽内容，禁止会员演唱或讲述可能危害公共道德性质的歌曲或故事。截至目前，该会经市社会局许可，已宣布禁止十六首歌曲或故事，并将向该局申请许可，将禁令扩展至另外三首，包括附件报告中提到的一首。

The following story was broadcasted at the
Li Zu Tuh Daung Broadcasting Station, No. 250 Burkill
Road by Tsu Sien Kung and Tsang Kei Yuin between 1.45
and 2.30 p.m. 28. 12. 36.

A girl named Zi Ah Tseng had a sweet-heart and
she was three months in pregnancy by this man. When
this man got married to another girl he came to inform
her about his marriage and advised her also to marry
another man. She worried about her being in pregnancy
and asked him what should she do. He advised her to
buy Zo liyang and Fai Mau from Chinese medicine shop and
place them in her navel and stick Chinese plaster over it.
He also advised her to buy a piece of grass known "Tai
Tsih Tsau" and insert same into her organ three inches
(one inch for each month of pregnancy). She would then
feel shivering cold and fever. Abortion is then succeeded.

In my opinion this sort of a story is very
objectional according to police point of view.

以下故事由徐先公（Tsu Sien Kung）和张奇云（Tsang Kei Yuin）于1936年12月28日下午1:45至2:30之间，在伯基尔路250号力祖特大当广播电台播送。

一个名叫 Zi Ah Tseng 的女孩有个情人，她怀了此人的孩子三个月。当此人娶了另一个女孩时，他来告知她自己的婚事，并建议她也嫁给另一个男人。她担心自己怀孕，问他该怎么办。他建议她去中药店买“佐料阳”（Zo liyang）和“飞毛”（Fai Mau），放在肚脐上，并贴上膏药。他还建议她买一种叫“太吉草”（Tai Tsih Tsau）的草，将其插入器官内三英寸深（怀孕每月对应一英寸）。随后她会感到寒战和发烧。堕胎即告成功。

依我看，从警方角度来看，这类故事非常令人反感。

page_data.en:
SYNOPSIS

If you don't behave properly you will suffer

On the 1st and 15th of the lunar moon, the gates
of the temples open; on both sides are kneeling a number
of down-hearted beggars.

I hold with my left hand a basket and shout "good
mesdames, would you give me a copper." "Thank you, mesdames
and gentlemen, I hope you will win the 1st prize of the
lottery tickets, be rich and live long."

Oh! There comes a big proprietor who dresses nicely
and appears to have good luck.

"Be pitiful on me," I cry, "I haven't had a bowl of
rice for the past few days and am starving to death."

The proprietor instead of giving me a copper reprimands
me and I cannot help bursting into tears. My parents treat-
ed me like a pet, I did not work but chose the best to eat
and dress, gambled and frequented brothels. All my pro-
perties are thus gone. When I began to repent I was already
a beggar.

At present I wear ragged clothes and have to go in snow and
rain.

I wish to advise you, big proprietors, to let your sons
learn a profession so that they may earn a living in future.
I, Woo Saung Ngan, having failed to learn a job during my
boyhood, am now compelled to become a comedian in order to
maintain my life.

情节概要

行为不端必将受苦

农历初一和十五，寺庙大门敞开；两侧跪着许多心灰意冷的乞丐。

我左手提着一个篮子，喊道：“好太太们，能给我一个铜板吗？”“谢谢太太先生们，祝你们彩票中头奖，富贵长寿。”

哦！来了一位大老板，衣着光鲜，看起来运气不错。

“可怜可怜我吧，”我哭喊道，“我过去几天没吃过一碗饭，快要饿死了。”

那位老板非但不给我铜板，反而斥责我，我不禁痛哭流涕。父母把我当宝贝宠着，我不工作，只挑最好的吃穿，赌博并 frequenting 妓院。我的所有财产就这样耗尽了。当我开始悔悟时，我已经是个乞丐了。

现在我衣衫褴褛，不得不风雪中奔波。

我想劝告各位大老板，让你们的儿子学一门手艺，以便将来谋生。我，何双年，因年少时未能学到一门手艺，现在被迫成为滑稽戏演员以维持生计。

With reference to the broadcasting of the story
entitled "Victim of Opium" in which it was alleged the victim
was maltreated by foreign policemen and warders, from the
Hua Hsing Broadcasting Station, 19 Tsingtao Road, between
5.15 p.m. and 6 p.m. December 29, 1936, by two comedians
named Woo Saung-ngan (何双景 ) and Sung Siau-ding
(沈笑亭 ), a copy of the synopsis of the story has been
obtained, and its translation is attached to this report. As
nothing is mentioned in the synopsis about the alleged maltreat-
ment, Woo Saung-ngan, one of the two comedians, was interviewed
on January 7, 1936, and asked for an explanation. In reply,
Woo admitted that the written synopsis was an amended one and
remarked that, strictly speaking, people of his profession
did not as a rule prepare synopsis word by word, but a brief
outline of the story.

With reference to the allegation against the foreign
policeman and warder, Woo admitted that it might have been
included in the story broadcasted on December 29, 1936, but
stated that during the last few days when the story was
re-broadcasted, all parts relating to the assault were omitted.
In conclusion Woo gave an assurance that he and his partner
would refrain from using such libellous remarks in stories in
future.

事由 关于青岛路19号华兴广播电台播出的题为“鸦片受害者”的广播节目。

由探员施子良（Sih Tse-liang）撰写 转呈 [签名]

关于1936年12月29日下午5时15分至6时之间，两名分别名为吴双景（何双景）和沈笑亭（沈笑亭）的滑稽戏演员，从青岛路19号华兴广播电台播出题为“鸦片受害者”的故事一事，故事中指控受害者遭到外籍警察和狱卒的虐待，现已获取该故事的情节概要副本，其译文附于本报告之后。由于情节概要中未提及所谓的虐待行为，遂于1936年1月7日约谈了两名滑稽戏演员之一的吴双景，并要求其作出解释。吴双景回答说，书面提交的情节概要是经过修改的版本，并评论说，严格来说，他们这一行的人通常不会逐字准备情节概要，而只是准备一个简短的故事大纲。

关于对外籍警察和狱卒的指控，吴双景承认这可能包含在1936年12月29日播出的故事中，但声称在最近几天重播该故事时，所有涉及袭击的部分均已被删去。最后，吴双景保证他和他的搭档今后将在故事中避免使用此类诽谤性言论。

吴双景和沈笑亭在过去十个月里一直在青岛路19号的华兴广播电台进行广播。他们的办公室位于福煦路附近贝勒路（Rue Amiral Bayle）道德里10号。

page_data.en:
Translation of the synopsis of the
story entitled "Victim of Opium"

One inch of time is worth one inch of gold, but with one inch of
gold, you cannot buy one inch of time. An old saying runs, "It is not
a strange thing to lose gold, but when you lose time, you can never
find it." I am a sick man. I am twenty six years old. I am
really a young man. My parents possess a great deal of money, and
love me dearly. My mother hopes that I may be able to earn my livelihood
when I grow up. When I am in my teens, I am lazy in learning a trade.
I indulge in eating, dressing myself in fine clothes, frequenting
brothels and in gambling. Incidentally, I become addicted to opium
smoking. At first I smoke opium as a pastime, but eventually the
habit becomes so strong that I cannot afford to live without smoking
opium three to five times a day. When the craving is not satisfied,
tears will run down my cheek. I have spent the property of my parents
on opium smoking and the habit has reduced me to a shadow of my
former robust self. My head resembles an electric bulb and my eyes
lotus seeds. My nose looks like a medicine bottle and my ears
bitter chestnuts. My mouth resembles a dumpling and my neck the handle
of a spoon. My arms look like foreign ginsengs. My legs resemble
two straw ropes. In the distance, I look like a dead frog and on
closer inspection I resemble a small monkey. Finally, my father
publishes an advertisement in the newspapers announcing the severance
of our relations as father and son. He drives me out of the family.
Once driven out, I suffer terribly. I do not care much about rice,
but I cannot live without opium. I borrow money from all my friends
and relatives and pawn all my clothes I have on. In the day time, I
beg alms on the streets; at night I stay in an opium den.

One day, two detectives arrest and send me to the Police Station.
I am later sent to a prison. A foreigner asks me why I, as a young
man, wish to become an opium addict and to make an ugly figure of
myself. When I was at home, I used to desire to go out. Now I am
imprisoned. In the summer, the prison is so hot that I can scarcely
stand it. In the winter, I have to sleep on the cold cement floor.
There are no stoves or steam heating in the prison. Every day, I have
to take a cold water bath. The bath is so terribly cold that I some
times cry for my life. The sufferings I receive are beyond description.
There is no body to whom I can complain of my sufferings. I have to
blame myself for contracting the habit of opium smoking. I am only
twenty six years of age, but my reputation has been damaged. As I am
not accustomed to the living conditions in the prison, I become sick
and later unconscious.

Opium is really a scourge to the people and has caused the death
of many persons. Since its introduction into China, thousands upon
thousands of people have become opium addicts. Their property is spent
on opium. Steamers and houses which they possess are sold to satisfy
their craving. Their wives become the wives of others and their sons
step-sons of others. Their daughters are sold to satisfy their
craving. The only things left to them are one opium pipe and one
opium lamp. I advise good brethren not to smoke opium so that they can
enjoy good health. If some of them have contracted the habit of
opium smoking, they must cure themselves of the evil at once. They
must show fortitude in getting rid of the habit.

In my case, I am very anxious to cure myself of the habit, because
I can no longer bear the attendant sufferings, but it is too late to
save my life.
page_data.zh:
题为“鸦片受害者”的故事
情节概要译文

一寸光阴一寸金，寸金难买寸光阴。古语云：“失金不为奇，失时不可追。”我是一个病人。我今年二十六岁。我确实是个年轻人。我的父母拥有大量钱财，并且非常疼爱我。母亲希望我长大后能自谋生计。在我十几岁时，我懒于学习手艺。我沉溺于美食、华服、逛妓院和赌博。顺便提一下，我染上了吸食鸦片的恶习。起初我吸鸦片只是为了消遣，但最终瘾头变得如此之大，以至于我每天不吸三到五次鸦片就无法生活。当烟瘾得不到满足时，我会泪流满面。我把父母的财产都花在吸食鸦片上，这个习惯使我原本强壮的身体变得形销骨立。我的头像电灯泡，眼睛像莲子。我的鼻子像药瓶，耳朵像苦栗子。我的嘴像饺子，脖子像勺柄。我的手臂像洋人参。我的腿像两根草绳。远看像一只死青蛙，近看像一只小猴子。最后，父亲在报纸上刊登广告，宣布断绝父子关系。他将我赶出家门。一旦被赶出家门，我便遭受极大的痛苦。我对米饭不太在意，但没有鸦片我就活不下去。我向所有的亲朋好友借钱，并典当身上所有的衣服。白天，我在街头乞讨；晚上，我住在鸦片馆里。

一天，两名侦探逮捕了我，并将我送到警察局。后来我被送进监狱。一个外国人问我，作为一个年轻人，为什么想成为鸦片烟鬼，把自己弄得面目可憎。在家时，我常常想出去。现在我被监禁了。夏天，监狱热得我几乎无法忍受。冬天，我必须睡在冰冷的水泥地上。监狱里没有火炉或蒸汽暖气。每天，我都必须洗冷水澡。洗澡水冷得可怕，有时我哭喊着求饶。我所受的苦难无法形容。没有人可以让我倾诉苦难。我只能责怪自己染上了吸食鸦片的恶习。我虽然只有二十六岁，但名誉已受损。由于我不习惯监狱的生活条件，我生病了，后来失去了知觉。

鸦片确实是人民的祸害，导致许多人死亡。自从传入中国以来，成千上万的人成为了鸦片烟鬼。他们的财产耗费在鸦片上。他们拥有的轮船和房屋被变卖以满足毒瘾。他们的妻子成了别人的妻子，儿子成了别人的继子。女儿被卖掉以满足毒瘾。留给他们的只有一根烟枪和一盏鸦片灯。我劝告各位好兄弟不要吸食鸦片，以便享受健康。如果有些人已经染上了吸食鸦片的恶习，必须立即戒除这一恶习。他们必须表现出毅力来摆脱这个习惯。

就我而言，我非常渴望戒除这个习惯，因为我再也无法忍受随之而来的痛苦，但挽救我的生命为时已晚。

"B" Divisional Office,
December 31st, 1936.

Sir,
Two comedians named Woo Sau Ngan and Sung Siau Ding
broadcasted a song known as "Victims of Opium" at Hua
Hsing Broadcasting Station, 19 Tsingtao Road between 5.15
and 6 p.m. December 29th, 1936.
The song describes a young man named Wong Ah Mau
who was from a rich family addicted to opium habit. In
consequence of this he was driven out of the family by
his parents. He was picked up one day by detectives from
a certain alleyway for smoking opium and taken to a police
station where he was beaten and kicked by a Foreign police-
man. He died shortly afterwards from injuries received but
revived again. On being taken to the Court he was convicted
and sent to the Municipal Gaol to undergo his punishment.
During confinement he was subjected to taking of cold baths
which is unbearable, kicked by foreign warders with foreign
boots and struck by Indian warders with butts of their rifles.
The song itself is good because it tells people not
to smoke opium or those who are addicts to get rid of this
habit as soon as possible, but the allegations against the
police and Gaol Authorities are absurd.

“B”分区办事处，
1936年12月31日。

先生，
两名名为吴双景（Woo Sau Ngan）和沈笑亭（Sung Siau Ding）的滑稽戏演员，于1936年12月29日下午5时15分至6时之间，在青岛路19号华兴广播电台播出一首名为“鸦片受害者”的歌曲。
这首歌描述了一个名叫黄阿毛（Wong Ah Mau）的年轻人，他出身富裕家庭，染上了鸦片烟瘾。因此，他被父母赶出家门。有一天，他在某条弄堂里因吸食鸦片被侦探抓获，并被带到警察局，在那里遭到一名外籍警察的殴打和脚踢。他随后因受伤不久后死亡，但又复活了。在被带上法庭时，他被定罪并送往公共租界监狱服刑。
在监禁期间，他被迫洗难以忍受的冷水澡，被外籍狱卒穿着外籍靴子踢打，并被印度狱卒用步枪枪托击打。
这首歌本身是好的，因为它告诫人们不要吸食鸦片，或者那些成瘾者尽快戒除这一习惯，但对警察和监狱当局的指控是荒谬的。

牙片烟害殺我同胞

一寸光陰一寸金。寸金难買寸光陰。老古话。失落黄金勿希
奇。失落光陰没處寻。那亭走出我生病人。想我生病人
年纪正二苦。想我年纪今年必过念六岁。正是一个年少
年少。想厄爷娘家当充阔度。厄爷：养我金和宝，厄姆妈养
玉和。希望我長度之後那细细寻。那晓得我一到十或岁
生意龙得勿肯做，到吃着赌门槛转。後收到把牙片
烟来吃上。起初吃了白相勿要紧。後收到吃得尼头深。一日
要三旦登。勿吃勿过门。就要眼泪涕出外个。那个爷娘毒当吃
干净。吃得我人像辣爪金。枯浪头像雪灯笼。眼睛像糖
连心。鼻头像只沙革瓶。耳朵像只沙角菱。嘴巴像只剪馄
饨。颈项为像扫走柄。臂巴捺根西洋参。大腿为像串颈绳。
远看为像哈蟆。近看为像小猢。後收来登报申明爷子
脱离关系。那我干去川。我一出门辛苦万分。白饭勿吃勿要紧。牙片
烟勿吃勿过门。祝娟朋友在借钏素。身浪衣裳当干净。日里马路浪向
讨细细。夜里烟子窠里去登身。有一日来之廿个包打听。那我巡捕
行事捉进。到避牢里向去登身。捉进要辛苦万分。外国人问我年纪
轻：还哼要吃牙片烟。牙片吃得勿像人，作孽侬我自作自受苦万分。
西为屋里叫勿要登。到如今一日到监牢里向登。热天登拉里向
热杀人。冷天则为登拉四门汀，呒不火爐老热水汀。每日起来
要汰冷水浴。冷得我薄拉嗙啷叫救命。末我吃之苦头去告诉
人拉啥人听。则怪我自家麼良心。那牙片吃上瘾，我今年年纪必

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE JAPANESE RADIO STATION XQHA

There is in Shanghai a Japanese radio
broadcasting station whose calling signal is XQHA.
According to newspaper reports, the programme of this
radio station is frequently interrupted by a strange wave
length.
According to the Director of the Shanghai
Telegraph Administration, this Japanese radio station has
no right to use its calling signal and wave length, nor
has it the right to operate as a radio broadcasting station,
because the management of this station, before it was
bought over by Japanese from the American owners, had
failed to secure the approval of the Ministry of
Communications. Following the illegal transfer of this
station to Japanese ownership, the Ministry of Communications
has withdrawn its calling signal and wave length. It is
learned that any legitimate radio station may now apply
to the Ministry of Communications for the use of the letters
XQHA as a calling signal and wave length No. 580.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

MR. WANG CHING WEI COMING TO SHANGHAI FEBRUARY 6

According to information secured from the
local residence of Mr. Chu Min Nyi, a member of the C.E.C.,
Mr. Wang Ching Wei, President of the Central Political
Council, will come to Shanghai on February 6 to attend to
various official and private affairs. Mr. Wang will not
remain long, because he has to return to Nanking to attend
the Third Plenary Session on February 15.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking Telegram) :-

GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK STILL IN HANGCHOW

On the afternoon of February 4, General and
Madame Chiang Kai Shek made an inspection of various districts
in Hangchow, after which they made a trip up to Wu San and
Chu Yang San Mountains.

According to the Central News Agency, Dr. H.
H. Kung, Minister of Finance, left Nanking for Shanghai by
train on the night of February 4.

1937年2月5日。 4. 晨间翻译。

原告提交的损害详情系捏造，陈发兹（Chen Fah Tse）现已向南市上海地方法院对这141人提起企图勒索的指控。由于所谓罪行发生在公共租界内，该案已由上海地方法院移交给上海第一特区地方法院。
昨天下午，陈发兹在上海第一特区地方法院接受戴荣鐸法官的讯问。案件延期审理。将对141名被告发出传票。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：

日本广播电台 XQHA

上海有一家日本广播电台，其呼号为XQHA。据报纸报道，该电台的节目经常受到奇怪波长的干扰。
据上海电政管理局局长称，这家日本广播电台无权使用其呼号和波长，也无权作为广播电台运营，因为该电台的管理层在被日本人从美国业主手中收购之前，未能获得交通部的批准。在该电台非法转让给日本所有者后，交通部已收回其呼号和波长。据悉，任何合法广播电台现在均可向交通部申请使用字母XQHA作为呼号以及580号波长。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

汪精卫先生将于2月6日抵沪

据中央执行委员会朱民谊（Chu Min Nyi）先生本地寓所得到的消息，中央政治会议主席汪精卫先生将于2月6日来沪处理各种公务和私事。汪先生不会停留太久，因为他必须返回南京参加2月15日的第三届全体会议。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：

蒋介石将军仍在杭州

2月4日下午，蒋将军和蒋夫人视察了杭州各区，随后前往吴山和玉皇山游览。

据中央通讯社报道，财政部长孔祥熙博士于2月4日晚乘火车离开南京前往上海。

page_data.en:
February 5, 1937.

MAINICHI

AMBASSADOR KAWAGOE LEAVING FOR NANKING

Ambassador Kawagoe will leave
for Nanking on February 6 or 8 to resume the Sino-Japanese
negotiations. Mr. Tajiri, First Class Secretary, left
for Nanking on the morning of February 4.

JOINT CONFERENCE OF JAPANESE CHAMBERS OF
COMMERCE IN CHINA

At 1 p.m. yesterday the Shanghai
Japanese Chamber of Commerce held a meeting at the Japanese
Club to consider the joint conference of all Japanese
Chambers of Commerce in China. The meeting decided to
hold the conference on March 11. It will last three days.
Chambers of Commerce in Japan will be invited to send
representatives to attend the joint conference in Shanghai.

CHINESE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS INTERRUPTS
PROGRAMME OF JAPANESE BROADCASTING STATION

It is reported that the broad-
casting by the Japanese station XQHA is being interrupted
by the Ministry of Communications. Mr. Pau, chief of the
local Government Telegraph Office, states that the station
XQHA, which was purchased by a Japanese from an American,
had not secured the approval of the Ministry of Communications
for the transfer, therefore, the transaction was illegal.
As the transfer is one concerning
Japanese and Americans, the Ministry of Communications has
no right to cancel the station's wave-length.

ESTABLISHMENT OF POST OFFICE ON JAPANESE SHIPS:
CHINESE POSTAL REGULATIONS NOT VIOLATED

In connection with the establish-
ment of a post office on the s.s. Shanghai Maru and the
s.s. Nagasaki Maru by the Japanese Ministry of Communications
for the benefit of both Japan and China, a certain Chinese
organ states that Japanese stamps are being sold on
the steamers. For this reason, the Chinese Post Office
sent Mr. Wong, an officer to make an investigation on the
ship.
Mr. Wong states that on
February 3 he visited the s.s. Nagasaki Maru. He declares
that the post office on the ship did not constitute a
violation of the Chinese Postal Regulations as Chinese
stamps were used on letters in accordance with
international Postal Law and no postal business was done
by the post office during the period that the ship was
moored at the wharf.

《每日新闻》

川越大使启程赴南京

川越大使将于2月6日或8日启程前往南京，以恢复中日谈判。一等秘书田尻先生已于2月4日上午启程赴南京。

在华日本商会联席会议

昨日下午1时，上海日本商工会议所在日本俱乐部举行会议，商讨在华所有日本商会的联席会议事宜。会议决定于3月11日举行该联席会议，会期三天。将邀请日本国内的商会派代表出席在上海举行的联席会议。

中国交通部中断日本广播电台节目

据报，日本电台XQHA的广播正受到交通部的干扰。当地政府电报局主管鲍先生称，XQHA电台由一名日本人从美国人手中购得，但未获得交通部对此次转让的批准，因此该交易属非法。由于此次转让涉及日本人和美国人，交通部无权取消该电台的波长。

在日本船只上设立邮局：未违反中国邮政条例

关于日本通信省为便利中日两国而在“上海丸”轮和“长崎丸”轮上设立邮局一事，某中国机构声称这些轮船上正在出售日本邮票。为此，中国邮政局派遣官员黄先生登船调查。
黄先生称，他于2月3日登上了“长崎丸”轮。他声明，船上的邮局并不构成对中国邮政条例的违反，因为根据国际邮政法，信件上使用的是中国邮票，且在船舶停泊码头期间，该邮局未办理任何邮政业务。

REPORT
Date March 4, 1937.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 203
Special Branch 4/3/37

Subject Eight local broadcasting stations ordered to cease
functioning.

Made by C.D.I. Sik Tse-liang Forwarded by Ibynu D.S.I

Six representatives of the six broadcasting stations
which ceased operations on February 2, 1937, by order of the
Chinese Telegraph Administration, and three representatives
of the Shanghai Municipality Broadcasting Station Owners'
Association, left Shanghai for Nanking on February 25. The
object of this delegation was to appeal to the Government
authorities for cancellation of the order affecting closure
of the above mentioned broadcasting stations, as well as the
order affecting all broadcasting stations, in general,
requiring them to devote one third of their broadcasting time
to educational programmes (Vide Special Branch Report dated
February 25, 1937). The delegation returned to Shanghai on
February 28.

According to Wong Wan-bah (王完白 ), Chairman of
the Broadcasting Station Owners' Association, the mission
resulted in failure. It is further learned that the Ministry
of Communications has instructed the Chinese Telegraph
Administration to buy over from the stations affected the
apparatus used by them in broadcasting, in order to relieve
them of financial loss. The order also intimates that the
educational programme might include semi-educational subjects,

Sik Tse-liang
C. D. I.

主题：八家本地广播电台奉令停止运作。

撰写人：C.D.I. 席子良 转呈人：Ibynu D.S.I

1937年2月2日，六家广播电台奉中国电信管理局命令停止运营，其六名代表以及上海市政广播电台业主协会的三名代表，于2月25日离开上海前往南京。该代表团的目的是向政府当局上诉，请求撤销影响上述广播电台关闭的命令，以及影响所有广播电台、要求其将三分之一广播时间用于教育节目的命令（参见1937年2月25日的特别处报告）。代表团于2月28日返回上海。

据广播电台业主协会主席王完白（Wong Wan-bah）称，此次使命以失败告终。另获悉，交通部已指示中国电信管理局从受影响的电台购买其用于广播的设备，以减轻其经济损失。该命令还暗示，教育节目可以包括半教育性质的科目，

March 2, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.

Lih Pao publishes the following telegraphic reports:

CERTAIN NATION ATTEMPTS TO CREATE DISTURBANCES IN
KWANGTUNG AND SHANTUNG PROVINCES

According to information received by the
Kwangtung Provincial authorities, certain nationals have
secretly entered Kwangtung Province to engage "white"
Russians to carry out certain plans. The provincial
authorities have instructed the military and police organs
to adopt strict precautionary measures against trouble.

Some 30 suspicious looking Japanese have
arrived at Tsingtao from Japan. Disguised as Chinese,
they have secretly gone to Chuen-Fu (曲阜), Lan-Yang
(莱阳), Tsing-Chow (青州), Tai-An (泰安) and
Chao-Chwang (枣庄) Hsiens in Shantung Province to
undertake certain activities. The provincial authorities
have notified the various Hsien authorities to pay close
attention to these activities.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

THE GOVERNMENT AND LOCAL BROADCASTING STATIONS

The Dong Loh (同樂) and five other broadcasting
stations have been ordered by the Chinese authorities to
close. The local Radio Broadcasting Station Owners'
Association the other day appointed three members of the
Standing Committee of the Association together with the
delegates of the six broadcasting stations to submit an
appeal to the Nanking authorities.
The representatives arrived at Nanking on
February 27 and submitted appeals to the Central Kuomintang
Headquarters, the Executive Yuan and the Supervisory
Yuan.
They were informed that the matter would be
referred to the competent organs to be dealt with according
to law and circumstances.
At the Ministry of Communications the
representatives were received by two departmental chiefs
and informed that adequate measures to cope with the six
broadcasting stations in question had been drawn up and
that the Shanghai Telegraph Administration had been
confidentially ordered to handle the matter on the basis
of these measures. The officials added that the Ministry
had no intention as yet to suppress certain broadcasting
stations.
As regards broadcasting programmes, another
departmental chief stated that proper stories, music, talks
etc. could be included in the educational programmes and
that short and simple advertisements could be broadcasted
either before or after the programmes. He added that
the programmes could be changed at any time and that measures
governing the issue of subsidies to broadcasting stations
would be devised and drawn up.
The representatives returned to Shanghai on
February 28.

1937年3月2日。
下午译件。

《立报》刊登以下电讯报道：

某国试图在广东和山东省制造骚乱

据广东省当局收到的消息，某些国民已秘密进入广东省，雇佣“白”俄人执行某些计划。省当局已指示军警机关采取严格的预防措施以防生变。

约30名形迹可疑的日本人从日本抵达青岛。他们伪装成中国人，秘密前往山东省的曲阜、莱阳、青州、泰安和枣庄各县进行某些活动。省当局已通知各县当局密切关注这些活动。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

政府与本地广播电台

同乐及其他五家广播电台已被中国当局责令关闭。本地无线电广播电台业主协会日前指派协会常务委员会的三名成员，连同六家广播电台的代表，向南京当局提交请愿书。
代表们于2月27日抵达南京，并向国民党中央党部、行政院和监察院提交了请愿书。
他们被告知，此事将移交主管机关，依法依情处理。
在交通部，代表们受到两位部门主管的接见，并获悉已制定应对这六家广播电台的适当措施，且上海电信管理局已接到密令，基于这些措施处理此事。官员们补充说，部里目前无意取缔某些广播电台。
关于广播节目，另一位部门主管表示，教育节目中可以包含适当的故事、音乐、谈话等，简短简单的广告可以在节目前后播出。他补充说，节目可以随时更改，并将制定和拟定向广播电台发放补贴的措施。
代表们于2月28日返回上海。

March 1, 1937. Morning Translation.

National Herald and other local newspapers :-

THE LOCAL BROADCASTING STATIONS

In technical matters, the local broadcasting stations are subject to the control of the Ministry of Communications, while the programmes they broadcast are under the supervision of the Broadcasting Business Directing Committee recently formed by the National Government.
All programmes must be submitted to the Directing Committee for approval before they can be broadcasted. Forty per cent of the programme must be devoted to educational subjects and sixty per cent to amusements. All programmes which do not comply with this rule are rejected by the Committee. Good results have been secured by the enforcement of the rule.
The Directing Committee is drawing up a time table, setting aside certain hours for the broadcasting of educational programmes and amusement programmes. The time table will be put into force at the end of March. The contents of the programmes will be decided by the broadcasting stations, but they will be subject to approval by the Directing Committee as before, and the proportion between the educational programme. and the amusement programme must be maintained.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

Mr. Wong Huai Pah (王完白) and other representatives detailed by the local Broadcasting Station Owners' Association to petition the National Government to rescind the order closing down eight local broadcasting stations returned to Shanghai from Nanking yesterday morning.
It is learned that the Ministry of Communications has promised to consider their petition.
A general meeting of the local Broadcasting Station Owners' Association will be held in the near future to discuss the situation.

Central China Daily News dated Feb.27:

THE OPIUM SUPPRESSION CAMPAIGN

The Ministry of Justice has issued a circular order to all Courths throughout the country to instruct Bar Associations to ascertain whether any of their members are opium smokers and to compel such members to resign from the Bar Association concerned. They will also be disbarred.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers :

BUDDHIST ASSOCIATION TO ENTERTAIN DR. RAO

The local Buddhists' Association will hold a meeting in a few days to welcome Dr. Rao, the noted Indian scholar. Dr. Rao will be requested to deliver an address.

《国民日报》及其他本地报纸：

本地广播电台

在技术事项上，本地广播电台受交通部管辖，而其播出的节目则受国民政府最近成立的广播事业指导委员会监督。
所有节目在播出前必须提交指导委员会批准。百分之四十的节目必须用于教育题材，百分之六十用于娱乐题材。所有不符合此规则的节目均被委员会驳回。执行该规则已取得良好效果。
指导委员会正在制定时间表，划出特定时段用于播出教育节目和娱乐节目。该时间表将于3月底生效。节目内容由各广播电台决定，但仍需像以前一样经指导委员会批准，且教育节目与娱乐节目的比例必须保持。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

王完白（Wong Huai Pah）先生及本地广播电台业主协会委派的其他代表，在向国民政府请愿撤销关闭八家本地广播电台的命令后，于昨晨从南京返回上海。
据悉，交通部已承诺考虑他们的请愿。
本地广播电台业主协会将于近期召开全体会议，讨论局势。

2月27日《华中日报》：

禁烟运动

司法部已向全国所有法院发出通令，指示律师公会查明其会员中是否有鸦片吸食者，并迫使此类会员辞去相关律师公会的职务。他们还将被取消律师资格。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

佛教协会宴请拉奥博士

本地佛教协会将于数日后举行会议，欢迎著名印度学者拉奥博士。将邀请拉奥博士发表演讲。

February 28, 1937.
Morning Translation
Sin Wan Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking :-

LOCAL BROADCASTING STATIONS

At 9 a.m. February 27, Mr. Wang Huai Pah(王完白)
and other representatives of the Shanghai Public Broadcasting
Station Owners' Association called on Mr. Oung Vung Hao
(翁文灝), Secretary-General of the Executive Yuan, and
requested:
(1) The withdrawal of the order prohibiting the
Sin Sun(新声), the Dong Loh(同樂) and six other radio
stations to broadcast programmes,
(2) The postponement of the period for the closing
of these stations so as to enable them to dispense with the
services of their employees if the Ministry of Communications
insists on their suppression in which event it is requested
that the Ministry take over the radio stations against
payment,
(3) The revision of the measures which stipulate
that half of the time of broadcasting should be devoted to
educational and amusement programmes, because such a scheme
would prove harmful to the business of radio stations.
Mr. Oung, the Secretary-General of the Executive
Yuan, promised to transmit their request to the Ministry of
Communications.
At 2 p.m. the same day, the representatives called
at the Ministry of Communications and submitted their appeal.
The representatives also submitted an appeal for assistance
to the Ministry of Industry. They left Nanking for Shanghai
by train the same day.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE MOTOR TRUCKS CARRYING FISH DEALERS

In view of the frequent occurrence of accidents,
involving motor trucks carrying fish dealers, due to negligence
on the part of the drivers, the Shanghai Fish Market has
drawn up certain measures. The Fish Market will summon the
representatives of the various motor truck hire companies to
an informal meeting to be held at the Market on March 2 to
discuss measures to prevent accidents.
The Fish Market has also written to the Shanghai
Bureau of Public Utilities and the Traffic Departments of
the French Police and the S.M.P. requesting them to draw up
regulations to prevent accidents involving trucks carrying
fish dealers, and to hold a monthly inspection of the engines
of the trucks.

THE POOTUNG FELLOW COUNTRYMEN'S ASSOCIATION

The Pootung Fellow Countrymen's Association publishes
an advertisement in to-day's issue of Min Pao and other local
newspapers announcing that a general meeting of members will
be held to-day (February 28) at which speeches and stage
performances will be given from 1 p.m. to 2.30 p.m.

THE WATER RATE QUESTION

The Real Estate Owners' Association will hold a
meeting at 3 p.m. to-day at its office to discuss the increase
in the water rate.

1937年2月28日。
上午译件
《新晚报》刊登以下来自南京的电讯：

本地广播电台

2月27日上午9时，上海公共广播电台业主协会的王完白（Wang Huai Pah）先生及其他代表拜会了行政院秘书长翁文灝（Oung Vung Hao）先生，并提出请求：
(1) 撤销禁止新声、同乐及其他六家电台广播节目的命令，
(2) 推迟这些电台的关闭期限，以便在交通部坚持取缔的情况下遣散员工；在此情况下，请求部方有偿接管这些广播电台，
(3) 修订规定一半广播时间应用于教育和娱乐节目的措施，因为此类方案将被证明有害于广播电台的业务。
行政院秘书长翁先生承诺将他们的请求转达给交通部。
同日下午2时，代表们拜访了交通部并提交上诉。代表们还向实业部提交了援助申请。他们于同日乘火车离开南京返回上海。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

载运鱼商的卡车

鉴于载运鱼商的卡车因司机疏忽而频繁发生事故，上海鱼市场已制定某些措施。鱼市场将召集各卡车租赁公司的代表，于3月2日在市场举行非正式会议，讨论预防事故的措施。
鱼市场还致函上海公用局以及法国警察部和工部局警务处的交通科，请求他们制定法规，以防止涉及载运鱼商卡车的事故，并对卡车发动机进行每月检查。

浦东同乡会

浦东同乡会在今天的《民报》及其他本地报纸上刊登广告，宣布将于今天（2月28日）举行会员大会，下午1时至2时30分将有演讲和舞台表演。

水费问题

地产业主协会将于今天下午3时在其办公室举行会议，讨论水费上涨事宜。

February 27, 1937.    2    Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ARREST OF MR. LIEU LOO YING

Mr. Lieu Loo Ying, a member of the C.E.C. of
the Kuomintang, was arrested on February 24 at the
Yangtsze Hotel in connection with the murder of General
Yang Yung Tai, former Chairman of the Hupeh Provincial
Government, and Mr. Tang Yu Jen, ex-Vice Minister of
Foreign Affairs. He is now being detained at Chengtu
Road Police Station and is favourably treated. His
meals are sent to him by his family and his wife visits
him occasionally. Persons who desire to see him must
first get permission from the Police Station and the
approval of Mr. Lieu himself. So far, he has
received only one or two visitors.
His case will be resumed on the morning of
March 1 when an application for his extradition will
be made by the Chinese authorities.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

THE GOVERNMENT AND LOCAL BROADCASTING STATIONS

Some time ago several local broadcasting stations,
namely Dong Loh (同樂), Chow Yu Kee (周協記), An Ding
(安定), Shih Ying (市音), Wei Ling (惠靈), Sin
Sun (新聲) and other radio broadcasting stations, were
ordered by the Ministry of Communications to cease
functioning.
In view of the fact that as these broadcasting
stations were established only after permission had been
secured from the Ministry of Communications in accordance
with the regulations of the Ministry governing the control
of public broadcasting stations, they must be regarded
as legitimate stations, and consequently they are entitled
to Government protection if they have not committed any
violation of the regulations.
As their petition to the Ministry of Communications
on February 4 requesting cancellation of the order and
the promulgation of measures relating to the standard
equipment of radio stations operated by the people has
been rejected, the entire body of local public
broadcasting stations have decided to cease broadcasting
to-day and will appoint representatives to proceed to
Nanking to appeal for assistance.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:

WU MEI'S SON RETURNS TO SHANGHAI

Lawyer Wu Mei (吳邁) was murdered at Hongkong
last month. His son, Wu Wei Ya (吳威亞), who went
to Hongkong to attend to the funeral of his father,
returned to Shanghai the other day.

1937年2月27日。    2    晨间译文。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

刘庐英先生被捕案

国民党中央执行委员刘庐英（Lieu Loo Ying）先生，因与前湖北省政府主席杨永泰将军及前外交部次长唐有壬先生被杀案有关，于2月24日在扬子饭店被捕。他现被拘押在成都路巡捕房，受到优待。其膳食由家属送来，其妻偶尔前往探视。欲见其人者，须先获巡捕房许可并经刘本人同意。截至目前，他仅接待过一两名访客。
此案将于3月1日上午复讯，届时中国当局将提出引渡申请。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

政府与本地广播电台

前此，同乐、周协记、安定、市音、惠灵、新声等数家本地广播电台奉交通部命令停止运营。
鉴于这些广播电台均是依照交通部关于管理公共广播电台的规定，在获得交通部许可后方才设立，故应视为合法电台；因此，若其未违反任何规定，理应受到政府保护。
由于它们于2月4日向交通部提出的请求撤销该命令并颁布关于民营广播电台标准设备措施的请愿书已被驳回，全体本地公共广播电台决定于今日停止播音，并将指派代表前往南京请愿求助。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

吴迈之子返沪

律师吴迈上月在香港遇害。其子吴威亚此前赴港料理父亲丧事，近日已返回上海。

February 26, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. M. P. C. I. D. No. D Date ... / ...）

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram) :-
GENERAL SUNG WEI SZ ARRIVES AT NANKING
General Sung Wei Sz, Chairman of the Shensi Provincial Government, in company with five Divisional Commanders of the North-East Army of General Chang Hsueh Liang's forces, arrived at Nanking on February 25 from Sian by aeroplane. In the evening, they called on Mr. Yu Yu Jen, President of the Control Yuan, and Dr. H.H. Kung, the Finance Minister. They will call on General Chiang Kai Shek on February 26. The five North-East Divisional Commanders will proceed to Fenghua to see General Chang Hsueh Liang.

Society Evening News :-
General Yu Han Mou, Pacification Commissioner of Kwangtung, and General Huang Sho Tso, Chairman of the Kwangsi Provincial Government, who attended the Third Plenary Session of the Kuomintang at Nanking, arrived in Shanghai at 7 a.m. February 25 by train. At 8.20 a.m. they proceeded to Hangchow. If time permits, they will leave for Fenghua to interview General Chang Hsueh Liang.
General Chiang Ting Wen, the Fukien Pacification Commissioner, returned to Shanghai yesterday from Fenghua after seeing General Chang Hsueh Liang.

Sun Huo Wan Pao :-
General Chang Hsueh Liang Proceeding to Nanking
Deeply grateful to the National Government for its generosity, General Chang Hsueh Liang is about to proceed to Nanking to offer his thanks.
General Chang and his wife went to Hangchow from Fenghua on February 25. After spending several days at Hangchow, General Chang will come to Shanghai en route to Nanking to call on General Chiang Kai Shek and General Ho Ying Chin, the War Minister, after which he will return to Shanghai for a stay.

Diamond (金鋼):-
LOCAL BROADCASTING STATION OWNERS PROCEEDING TO NANKING TO-DAY
Eight local broadcasting stations were recently ordered to suspend operations. Some days ago, the authorities announced that nine other broadcasting stations will be ordered to close down because they are improperly equipped.
The news came as a great surprise to the owners of local broadcasting stations. Their business will suffer heavily if the order of the Government that 40% of a broadcasting programme must be devoted to amusements and 60% to educational matters is enforced.

（批：D 18/9）

《大公报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：
宋维泗将军抵达南京

陕西省政府主席宋维泗（Sung Wei Sz）将军，偕同张学良将军部队东北军的五位师长，于2月25日乘飞机从西安抵达南京。当晚，他们拜谒了监察院院长于右任先生和财政部长孔祥熙博士。他们将于2月26日拜谒蒋介石将军。这五位东北军师长将前往奉化会见张学良将军。

《社会晚报》：

PROTEST AGAINST ATROCITIES COMMITTED BY ITALIAN OFFICIALS
AND MARINES

When the Isis Theatre on North Szechuen Road
was screening the picture "Abyssinia" on February 20,
the local Italian Vice-Consul and the Commercial Attache,
leading some 300 armed Italian marines and civilians,
attacked the theatre, spread ammonia in the hall, destroyed
the film and assaulted the spectators. Several tens of
persons were injured.
The Isis Theatre is located in the extra-
Settlement road area and is under the jurisdiction of the
Chinese authorities. The attack constitutes contempt
towards China's Police rights and is an act of hostility
towards the 3,000,000 Chinese people in Shanghai.
The film in question was censored and approved
by the Central Film Censorship Committee. The interference
by the Italian officials and marines with the exhibition
of this picture constitutes a reflection upon the Film
Censorship Committee and impairs the dignity and sovereign
rights of China.
The Chinese Government should lodge a strong
protest with the Italian authorities and demand that an
apology be tendered to our Government, that the offenders
be deported and that compensation be paid. The Chinese
residents here should demand that the highest local Italian
authorities tender a separate apology to them and that
an assurance be given that similar incidents will not occur
again.
Chinese in various walks of life should
express their views.

抗议意大利官员及海军陆战队暴行

2月20日，当四川北路伊西斯大戏院放映电影《阿比西尼亚》时，当地意大利副领事和商务参赞率领约300名武装意大利海军陆战队员及平民袭击了该戏院，在大厅内喷洒氨水，损毁胶片并殴打观众。数十人受伤。
伊西斯大戏院位于越界筑路区域，受中国当局管辖。此次袭击构成对中国警察权的蔑视，也是对上海300万中国人民的敌对行为。
涉案影片业经中央电影检查委员会审查批准。意大利官员及海军陆战队干涉该片放映，是对电影检查委员会的侮辱，并有损中国的尊严与主权权利。
中国政府应向意大利当局提出强烈抗议，并要求其向我国政府道歉，驱逐肇事者并进行赔偿。在沪中国居民应要求当地意大利最高当局单独向他们道歉，并保证不再发生类似事件。
各界华人应发表意见。

Date....Feb....25....1937.

Subject........Eight broadcasting stations in the environs of
Shanghai ordered to cease operations.

Made by C.D.I....Sih Tse-liang........Forwarded by....J Boyce D A I

Further to the report dated February 4, 1937,
regarding the eight local broadcasting stations which ceased
operations on February 2 on the instructions of the Chinese
Telegraph Administration, because they were improperly
equipped and their broadcasting interfered with that of other
stations, the owners of two of these concerns, namely, the
Deng Fan and Hwa Kwang Stations, have decided to close down.
Six representatives from each of the remaining
stations, together with three from the Shanghai Broadcasting
Station Owners' Association (323 Kiangse Road) will leave
Shanghai for Nanking separately to-day, February 25, where
they will assemble and petition the Government authorities
to cancel the order prohibiting the stations from broadcasting.
Information has also been received that, apart from
the above matter, the representatives will request the
Government authorities to cancel another order, which the
stations recently received from the Ministry of Communications,
instructing that the daily broadcasting must not exceed 12
hours and that one third of the time should be devoted to
educational programmes and the remainder for amusement and
advertisement purposes. The owners complain that this
system is financially impracticable because, if it is enforced,
the time devoted to advertisement will be less, thus reducing
the income of the stations.
In order to show their unanimous support to the
delegation to Nanking, the owners of local broadcasting
stations who are members of the Shanghai Broadcasting Station
Owners' Association, have decided to suspend broadcasting for
one day on February 27, 1937.
Sih Tse-liang

制作人 刑事侦缉员....施子良........转呈人....J Boyce 助理督察

继1937年2月4日关于八家本地广播电台的报告之后，这些电台因设备不合格且广播干扰其他电台，奉中国电信管理局指令于2月2日停止运营。其中两家机构，即登丰电台和华光电台的业主，已决定关闭。
其余各电台各派六名代表，连同上海广播电台业主协会（江西路323号）的三名代表，将于今日（2月25日）分别离开上海前往南京，在那里汇合并向政府当局请愿，要求撤销禁止各电台广播的命令。
另获悉，除上述事项外，代表们还将请求政府当局撤销另一项命令，该命令是各电台近期从交通部收到的，指示每日广播不得超过12小时，其中三分之一时间应用于教育节目，其余时间用于娱乐和广告。业主们抱怨该制度在财务上不可行，因为若强制执行，用于广告的时间将减少，从而降低电台收入。
为显示对赴京代表团的一致支持，身为上海广播电台业主协会会员的本地广播电台业主决定于1937年2月27日停播一天。

China Times and other local newspapers :-

THE LOCAL BROADCASTING STATIONS

In February the Ministry of Communications
ordered the Dong Loh (同樂), the Sin Sun (新聲), the Tseu
Ya Kee (周協記), the Shih Ying (市音), the Wei Ling
(惠靈), the An Ding (安定), the Tung Peng (敦本) and
the Hwa Kwang (華光) Radio Broadcasting Stations in Shanghai
to cease functioning as they were improperly equipped and
were interfering with the broadcasting by other stations.
The Ministry also issued an order to other broadcasting
stations to the effect that the period of broadcasting must
not exceed 12 hours a day, that all broadcasting must cease
at midnight and that half of the time of broadcasting should
be devoted to educational and amusement programmes.
With the exception of the Tung Peng and the Hwa
Kwang, the eight stations which have been ordered to cease
operations have asked the Broadcasting Station Owners'
Association to request the Ministry of Communications to
rescind the order on the ground that the Ministry had
approved their establishment; that they had never interfered
with other stations; that all their equipment would become
useless and a number of persons would become unemployed
should the stations be forced to close. They requested
that, if the Ministry of Communications insisted that they
should close down their stations, their equipment be bought
over by the Ministry.
Regarding the order for a 20 minute broadcast
of educational programme and 40 minutes of amusement programme,
the Broadcasting Station Owners' Association expresses the
opinion that this is financially impracticable because the
income from advertisements will be reduced while the stations
will have to expend a large sum of money on lecturers for
the educational programmes.
Mr. Wang Wan Bah (王完白) and two other
representatives of the Broadcasting Station Owners' Asso-
ciation, together with representatives of six other broad-
casting stations, will proceed to Nanking to petition the
Ministry of Communications and the Central Directing Committee
in regard to this matter.

An entertainment was given to the press by the
Broadcasting Station Owners' Association at the Grand Hotel,
Thibet Road, yesterday at which Mr. Wang Wan Bah, Chairman
of the Association, made a report on these matters.
Mr. Wang also said that all broadcasting stations
which are members of the Association will cease functioning
on Saturday, February 17.

本地广播电台

交通部于二月命令上海的同乐、新声、周协记、市音、惠灵、安定、敦本和华光广播电台停止运营，理由是这些电台设备不合格，且干扰其他电台的广播。交通部还向其他广播电台发布命令，规定广播时间每天不得超过12小时，所有广播必须在午夜停止，且一半的广播时间应用于教育和娱乐节目。

除敦本和华光两家外，被勒令停业的八家电台已请求广播电台业主协会向交通部申请撤销该命令，理由如下：交通部曾批准其设立；它们从未干扰其他电台；如果被迫关闭，所有设备将报废，并导致多人失业。它们请求，如果交通部坚持要求关闭电台，则由交通部收购其设备。

关于播出20分钟教育节目和40分钟娱乐节目的命令，广播电台业主协会表示，这在财务上不可行，因为广告收入将减少，而电台必须花费巨资聘请教育节目的讲师。

王完白先生及广播电台业主协会的另外两名代表，连同其他六家电台的代表，将前往南京，就此事项向交通部和中央指导委员会请愿。

The 22 representatives who proceeded to Nanking

THE SHANGHAI RADIO STATION OF THE MINISTRY
OF COMMUNICATIONS

The Shanghai Radio Station of the Ministry of
Communications has erected a pair of big, new aerial masts
at the corner of Bubbling Well Road and Yates Road.
The new radio station will begin operations next
month. The power of the old station is 500 kilowatts but
the power of the new station will be 2,000 kilowatts

Eight Radio Stations Suppressed

By order of the Ministry of Communications, the
Tung Peng (敦本) and 7 other radio broadcasting stations
in this locality have been suppressed since February 1 this
year.
Yesterday the Shanghai Telegraph Administration
issued a formal circular notice to the effect that the
permits for the eight radio stations in question were
nullified on February 1 this year and that in future no
station will be allowed to use the calling signals and the
wave lengths of the suppressed radio stations without the
approval of the Ministry of Communications.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:

RUMOURS OF INCREASE IN MUNICIPAL RATE

Rumours were rife recently that the S.M.C. would
increase the Municipal Rate by 2%. Various circles raised
an opposition on the ground of trade depression.
According to information secured from the S.M.C.,
the Council has not yet come to any definite decision, and it
is, therefore, probable that there will be no increase in the
Municipal Rate.

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, JANUARY 21, 1934.

RADIO ELIMINATION

THE Greater Shanghai Radio Broadcasters' Association
is not likely to command a general sympathetic hear-
ing for its proposed protest against the order of the Min-
istry of Communications to cancel the permits of eight local
broadcasting stations. Admittedly the cancellation will
cost the stations so affected a few thousand dollars of
outlay, and yet the sacrifice, if sacrifice it were, may have
to be borne for the greater good of the business as a
whole.

Radio fans in Shanghai, we are sure, will agree with
the Ministry that some of the stations are more of a
nuisance than an attraction on the air. They occupy wave
lengths which might be utilised to better advantage by
stations more adequately equipped mechanically and from
the standpoint of talent.

It may be also remembered that the Ministry is con-
cerned not only with the quality of broadcasting but also
with the subject matter, which constitutes the entertain-
ment fare. On this point opinions will naturally differ.
Some will doubtless maintain that the public is entitled to
enjoy what it pleases and that the process of elimination
may be accomplished by public patronage or refusal of
patronage. On the other hand, the Ministry is properly
holding itself responsible for the educational value and in-
fluence of radio programs for the simple reason that they
hold an appeal alike to the educated and the uneducated,
the adults and the children of an impressionable age.

If a station—and we are not referring particularly to
the stations in question—should fail in maintaining a
minimum technical standard and in providing suitable pro-
grams acceptable to the authorities, it is no longer entitled
to enjoy the privileges embodied in an official permit. The
Government, one cannot deny, has the right to administer
what goes on in the air as what goes into print in a news-
paper. In both cases the principle of good morals holds
equal sway, and there is not the slightest authority any-
where for disputing such a right when properly exercised.

In a practical sense the elimination of undeserving
radio stations should go a long way toward stabilizing the
local business. As pointed out by Mr. Orlando Pao,
Director of the Shanghai Telegraph Office, the number of
radio stations in Shanghai is altogether too large for its
requirements. In New York it is only 8 while in Shanghai
it has reached 43.

As the result of the mushroom growth competition has
become unduly and unhealthily keen. The amount of
advertising revenue which the mercantile community is
able to contribute is perforce limited, especially in these
days of trade depression, and when it is divided among
a multitude of stations the share which one station may
partake is necessarily also limited. The paucity of revenue
must be counted as one of the most potent factors which
have retarded the development of radio broadcasting in
Shanghai and which have made it difficult, if not impossi-
ble, to employ professional artists to go on the air.

If the Ministry of Communications should continue to
apply its pruning process by easy stages, only the best
stations from all angles, will ultimately be allowed to
remain in the field. Then it may be possible for each of
them to earn sufficient revenue to offer programs, if
not of equal quality with those in the Occident, at least
deserving of genuine public appreciation which has thus
far been withheld for records reproduced.

From local sources there may be latent talent which
may be profitably developed and that requires an initial
outlay which, we are sure, no station here is yet prepared
to incur. With the gradual removal of the unfit and with
more revenue accruing to each surviving station such de-
velopment may come within the realm of practicability.

Thus it may be seen that in revoking eight licenses
the Ministry is embarking upon a sound policy by which
the best stations will eventually be benefited, and with
them the radio public here and everywhere.

《字林西报》，1934年1月21日，星期日。

取缔无线电广播

大上海无线电广播业同业公会拟就交通部下令吊销八家本地广播电台执照一事提出抗议，此举恐怕难以获得普遍的同情与支持。诚然，吊销执照将使受影响的电台损失数千美元的投入，然而，如果这算是一种牺牲的话，为了整个行业的更大利益，这种牺牲或许是必须承受的。

我们可以肯定，上海的无线电爱好者会赞同交通部的观点，即某些电台在空中电波中带来的困扰多于吸引力。它们占用的波长，本可以由那些在机械设备和人才方面配备更完善的电台加以更有效的利用。

此外还应记得，交通部关注的不仅是广播的质量，还有构成娱乐内容的题材。在这一问题上，意见自然会有分歧。无疑有人会坚持认为，公众有权享受其所喜爱之物，淘汰过程可以通过公众的支持或拒绝支持来实现。另一方面，交通部正确地承担起对广播节目教育价值和影响的责任，原因很简单，因为这些节目对受过教育者和未受教育者、成年人以及处于易受影响年龄的儿童都具有吸引力。

如果一家电台——我们并非特指涉事的那些电台——未能维持最低的技术标准，并提供当局认可的适宜节目，它便不再享有官方执照所赋予的特权。不可否认，政府有权管理空中传播的内容，正如管理报纸刊登的内容一样。在这两种情况下，良好道德的原则具有同等的约束力，只要正当行使这一权利，在任何地方都绝无质疑其合法性的依据。

从实际意义上讲，取缔不合格的广播电台将大大有助于稳定本地行业。正如上海电报局局长包尔兰多（Orlando Pao）先生所指出的，上海的广播电台数量相对于其需求而言实在过多。纽约仅有8家，而上海已达43家。

由于如雨后春笋般激增，竞争变得过度激烈且不健康。商界能够提供的广告收入总额必然有限，尤其是在当前贸易萧条时期，当这笔收入被众多电台分摊时，每家电台所能获得的份额自然也受到限制。收入匮乏必须被视为阻碍上海无线电广播发展的最有力因素之一，这也使得雇佣专业艺人进行广播变得困难，甚至不可能。

如果交通部继续分阶段实施其整顿措施，最终只允许各方面最优秀的电台留在行业内。届时，各家电台或许能够获得足够的收入，以提供虽未必能与西方节目质量媲美、但至少值得公众真正欣赏的节目，从而改变目前仅靠播放唱片维持的局面。

本地可能蕴藏着有待开发的人才，但这需要初始投入，我们相信目前的本地电台尚无一家准备承担这笔费用。随着不合格者的逐步淘汰，以及每家幸存电台收入的增加，这种发展可能会进入切实可行的领域。

由此可见，交通部吊销八家执照的做法是推行一项健全的政策，最终将使最优秀的电台受益，进而使本地及各地的无线电听众受益。

Min Pao and other local newspapers:-

THE CLOSING OF EIGHT RADIO STATIONS

The managements of the eight radio broadcasting
stations which were ordered by the Shanghai Telegraph
Administration of the Ministry of Communications to cease

assistance.

January 24, 1937. Morning Translation.

National Herald and other local newspapers:-

EIGHT LOCAL RADIO STATIONS ORDERED TO CEASE OPERATIONS

The eight local radio broadcasting units, namely the Teng Peng (敦本), the Hwa Kwang (華光), the Wei Ling (惠靈), the Chow Ya Kee (周協记), the Sin Sun (新声), the Dong Loh (同樂), the Shih Ying (市音) and the An Ting (安定) Radio Stations, which have been ordered by the Ministry of Communications to cease operations at the end of January, have requested the Radio Broadcasting Station Owners' Association to point out to the Ministry that they received the approval of the Ministry when they were first established and further that there were no regulations governing the equipments of radio stations. The Radio Broadcasting Station Owners' Association has submitted a telegraphic petition to the Ministry of Communications asking it to publish regulations governing the equipments of radio stations, and will hold a meeting of the Standing Committee on Wednesday, January 27, to discuss the matter. The eight broadcasting stations will also hold a meeting.

January 22, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:-

EIGHT LOCAL RADIO STATIONS ORDERED TO SUSPEND OPERATIONS

With a view to intruducing improvements in
local radio broadcasting and as a result of an investigation
recently made, the Ministry of Communications has instructed
the Shanghai Telegraph Administration to order, through the
medium of the local Radio Broadcasting Station Owners'
Association, eight local radio stations, namely the Teng
Peng ( 放本 ), the Hwa Kwang ( 華光 ), the Wei Ling ( 惠靈 ),
the Chow Ya Kee ( 周協記 ), the Sin Sun ( 新聲 ), the Dong
Loh ( 同樂 ), the Shih Ying ( 市音 ) and the An Ting ( 安定 ),
to cease operations by the end of this month, on the grounds
that these stations are not properly equipped.
It is learned that there are two causes
leading to this suspension order; first, the Ministry of
Communications considers that it is necessary to reduce the
number of stations in Shanghai, as certain complications
regarding wave-lengths are arising, and secondly, in addition
to two radio stations which are to be ordered to cease
operations on account of special reasons, the remaining
six are inadequately fitted.
According to the Shanghai Radio Broadcasting
Station Owners' Association, the above-mentioned eight
radio stations have submitted reports to the Association
requesting it to petition the authorities for relief.

January 22, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

The Social Daily News publishes the following poem written by one Loh Vung Kwan :-

"FROM TO-DAY"

From to-day, we should not remain apathetic
as we were formerly!
From to-day, we should not overlook our
duty of avoiding national extinction!
The prosperity of our nation depends entirely
upon our own strenuous efforts and endeavours!
Ah! China to-day is not the sleepy lion as
she was formerly!
She is now united whilst her people have
become energetic!
We should work for our nation!
Fear no guns or aeroplane bombs!
Let our vanguards offer their blood
To overthrow all those who are ferocious
and aggressive,
And to recover our territory in the North-east!
The North-east will forever belong to us!
Let us work energetically and strenuously
and fight!

The "Society Evening News" (社會晚報) published the following article on Jan.21:

BARBAROUS ACTIVITIES OF ENEMY IN THE NORTH-EAST

Owing to the fact that volunteers have been concealing themselves in every village in the North-east, our enemy recently set fire to houses in small villages, thus rendering them vacant and waste land resulting in the volunteers now having no further opportunities of employing them as hiding places. Most of the poor people ran for their lives to larger villages, and as they were unable to find accommodation, they were compelled to sleep and live in the open air. All became ill and were unable to obtain medicine for curative purposes.
Of late our enemy has had plots of land surrounded by wooden posts, in which a number of hungry dogs are placed. It is reported that the above mentioned poor people who were sick, but not yet dead were dragged into these plots to be used as food for the dogs. Pitiable human shrieks were audible at night time.

“从今天起”

从今天起，我们不应像从前那样冷漠！
从今天起，我们不应忽视避免国家灭亡的责任！
我们国家的繁荣完全取决于我们自己的努力和奋斗！
啊！今天的中国已不再是从前那头沉睡的狮子！

去推翻所有凶残和侵略者，
并收复我们在东北的领土！
东北永远属于我们！
让我们精力充沛、努力奋斗并战斗！

《社會晚報》于1月21日刊登了以下文章：

敌人在东北的野蛮行径

由于志愿人员隐藏在东北的每个村庄里，我们的敌人最近放火烧毁了小村庄的房屋，使其变成空地和不毛之地，导致志愿人员再也没有机会利用这些地方作为藏身之处。大多数穷人为了逃命跑到大村庄，由于找不到住所，他们被迫露宿野外。所有人都病倒了，且无法获得药物进行治疗。
最近，我们的敌人用木桩围起地块，里面放置了许多饿狗。据报道，上述患病但尚未死亡的穷人被拖进这些地块，作为狗的食物。夜间可以听到可怜的 human shrieks（人类尖叫声）。
