SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. REGISTRY.
No. D
January 22, 1937. Afternoon Translation

Peng(敦本), the Hwa Kwang(華光), the Wei Ling(奧靈),
the Chow Ya Kee(周協記), the Sin Sun(新聲), the Dong
Loh(同樂), the Shih Ying(市音) and the An Ting(安定),
to cease operations by the end of this month, on the grounds
that these stations are not properly equipped.
It is learned that there are two causes
leading to this suspension order; first, the Ministry of
Communications considers that it is necessary to reduce the
number of stations in Shanghai, as certain complications
regarding wave-lengths are arising, and secondly, in addition
to two radio stations which are to be ordered to cease
operations on account of special reasons, the remaining
six are inadequately fitted.
According to the Shanghai Radio Broadcasting
Station Owners' Association, the above-mentioned eight
radio stations have submitted reports to the Association
requesting it to petition the authorities for relief.

Investigation into the standard of education of local
radio artistes completed

In view of the fact that the standard of
education received by the local radio artistes and the
programmes they broadcast have immediate effects on the
life and thoughts of the public, the Shanghai Telegraph
Administration recently issued forms to be filled in by
radio artistes with the special object of ascertaining
their standard of education. As a result of these measures,
the Administration has found that out of a total number of
457 artistes, 159 have received private teaching, 99 have
studied in primary schools, 120 are middle school graduates
whilst only 18 have received university education; the
remaining 61 are illiterate.

Shanghai Kwangtung Pao (上海廣東報) publishes the following
article:

JANUARY 28TH

January 28, the day on which the Chinese
people embarked on the glorious war against Imperialism
and against Japan, is approaching. It was the day on
which sad but honourable events occurred. It was the
day on which the Chinese people armed to defend themselves
and caused the Capitalist Nations of the world and the
Japanese Imperialists to tremble. The bloody struggle
on January 28 smashed to pieces the ridiculous prediction
that China would be conquered in three days and disproved
the reliability of superior armaments. On January 28,
the movement of all small and weak nations to save
themselves from ruin commenced. The resistance offered
by the Chinese masses and soldiers on January 28 represents
the most brilliant deed in the history of China.

敦本（Peng）、華光（Hwa Kwang）、奧靈（Wei Ling）、周協記（Chow Ya Kee）、新聲（Sin Sun）、同樂（Dong Loh）、市音（Shih Ying）及安定（An Ting），因这些电台设备不当，须于本月底停止运营。
据悉，此项停播令有两个原因：首先，交通部认为有必要减少上海的电台数量，因为波长方面出现了一些复杂情况；其次，除了因特殊原因被勒令停播的两家电台外，其余六家电台设备不足。
据上海无线电广播业同业公会称，上述八家电台已向公会提交报告，请求公会向当局请愿以求宽免。

本地无线电艺员教育程度调查完毕

鉴于本地无线电艺员所受的教育程度及其播出的节目对公众的生活和思想有直接影响，上海电政管理局最近发出表格，供无线电艺员填写，以专门查明其教育程度。通过这些措施，管理局发现，在总共457名艺员中，159人接受过私人教学，99人曾在小学就读，120人为中学毕业生，而仅有18人受过大学教育；其余61人为文盲。

1月28日

1月28日，即中国人民投身于反对帝国主义和反对日本的光荣战争之日，即将来临。那是发生悲惨但光荣事件的日子。那是中国人民武装自卫，使世界资本主义国家和日本帝国主义者感到战栗的日子。1月28日的血腥斗争粉碎了中国将在三天内被征服的荒谬预言，并证明了优越武器的可靠性并非绝对。1月28日，所有弱小国家拯救自身免于毁灭的运动开始了。1月28日中国民众和士兵进行的抵抗，代表了中国历史上最光辉的事迹。

12th, August, 1937.

Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

I beg to forward attached 'order' (to myself) to obtain
a copy of a photograph of a former member of the Special Police
who is a partner in the Overseas Chinese Broadcasting Station.
Originally a search warrant was issued against the
broadcasting station. This was referred by me to the Municipal
Advocate on account of the nature of the alleged offence, i.e.
non-compliance with Broadcasting Regulations. Subsequently the
search warrant was passed to the Special Branch but execution
could not be effected as the United States Consular officials
were prepared to recognise the station as coming within their
jurisdiction.
A summons against a partner - the man mentioned in the
attached - was later issued, but this could not be served by the
Special Branch, who will have full details of the case on file.
Will you please forward a copy of the photograph in
question - or otherwise as you may see fit - direct to me,
together with attached Court Order.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant.

N. White.
Officer-in-Charge.

Made by D. S. Larby Forwarded by C. Crawford

With reference to summons No. 2884, issued by the
Shanghai First Special District Court at the instance of
the Shanghai Telegraph Office (Ministry of Communications)
against Tsung Zae Tuh (曾侍德 ), I have to state that detectives
attached to Bubbling Well Station and the Special Branch
visited House No. 23, Lane 1729, Avenue Road - the residence
of Tsung Zae Tuh - at 4.20 p.m., 29.7.37, when Tsung was
absent, and again at 7.30 p.m., 29.7.37, when he was present,
in an endeavour to serve the aforementioned summons on Tsung.
Tsung, who is usually known as Earle Chang, however,
refused to accept the summons on the grounds that he is a
British Canadian subject, having been born in Vancouver, B.C.
When it was pointed out that he is not registered at H.B.M.
Consulate-General as a British subject, Tsung stated that he
had endeavoured to register himself as such in 1933 but had
been informed by an official of the Consulate-General that
the procedure was unnecessary in view of the fact that he was
a Chinese. As further proof of his nationality, Tsung stated
that he had twice been summonsed and convicted by H.B.M. Court
in respect of charges of breaches of traffic regulations.
Subsequent enquiries, however, have revealed that this
individual has appeared before H.B.M. Court on one occasion,
3.11.36, when he was convicted for committing a breach of the
traffic regulations. It has also been learned that on the
8.8.35 and again on the 8.11.35, Tsung appeared before the
Shanghai First Special District Court and received convictions
in connection with offences similar to the above.
This information was therefore brought to the notice of
Mr. R. S. Heaney, Passport Officer of H.B.M. Consulate-General,

关于上海第一特区地方法院应上海电报局（交通部）之请求针对 Tsung Zae Tuh (曾侍德 ) 签发的第2884号传票，本人谨陈述如下：静安寺捕房及特务科的侦探于1937年7月29日下午4时20分前往爱文义路1729弄23号——即 Tsung Zae Tuh 的住所——当时 Tsung 不在家；随后又于1937年7月29日下午7时30分再次前往，当时他在场，试图向 Tsung 送达上述传票。然而，Tsung 通常被称为 Earle Chang，他以自己是英籍加拿大公民、出生于不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华为由，拒绝接受传票。当指出他并未在英国驻华总领事馆注册为英国臣民时，Tsung 称他曾在1933年尝试以此身份注册，但被告知鉴于他是华人，此程序并无必要。作为其国籍的进一步证明，Tsung 称他曾两次因违反交通法规被英国法院传唤并定罪。然而，随后的调查显示，此人仅于1936年11月3日一次出庭英国法院，并因违反交通法规被定罪。还获悉，Tsung 曾于1935年8月8日及1935年11月8日两次出庭上海第一特区地方法院，并因类似上述罪行被定罪。

With regard to the attached Search Warrant No. 2441
issued by Judge Feng of the Shanghai First Special District

and Huene K. Lowe (刘光墺 ) who are interested in the venture

Herbert Moy is an American citizen born in New York
City on 20 July 1911 and is in possession of American passport

Herbert Moy 是美国公民，1911年7月20日出生于纽约市，持有1932年10月19日在纽约签发的美国护照第560842号，并在上海美国领事馆注册，自1932年11月23日起居住于此。

Earle Chang 是英籍加拿大公民，1902年9月10日出生于不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华，持有1933年10月3日在渥太华签发的加拿大护照第66052号。他尚未在上海英国领事馆注册，但打算近期办理。

Huene K. Lowe 是英籍加拿大公民，1911年3月16日出生于不列颠哥伦比亚省维多利亚，持有1934年2月28日在渥太华签发的加拿大护照第72773号。他上次在上海英国领事馆注册是在1936年10月2日，但本年度尚未注册。

Application has already been filed with the American
Consulate for registration of the Overseas Broadcasting Company
as an American concern and whilst actual registration is still
pending owing to a technical difficulty concerning the use of
the Chinese language in some of the broadcasts, the Station
and nationality of the principal investor have been duly
recorded by the American Authorities who are, therefore,
prepared to extend full Consular protection to the principal
investor in view of the American interests involved. It is
believed that when the two British investors have duly
registered themselves with their Consulate that they will
received the same protection of the British Consulate.

The station in question was established as a business
venture and the principals now find that strict observance of
the regulations of the Ministry of Communications jeopardises
the popularity of the station with its regular advertisers from
whom much of the income is derived. They have, therefore,
ceased to observe the requirements of the Ministry of Communications
who recently lodged a complaint with the American Consul against
the activities of the station. It is believed that on this
occasion the American Authorities made their attitude in the
matter quite clear to the Chinese Authorities.

M. Lanier
D.S.I.
Forwarded together with copy of
report forwarded to C. I. White.

已向美国领事馆提交申请，将海外广播公司注册为美国企业，虽然由于部分广播中使用中文的技术困难，实际注册仍在 pending 状态，但该电台及主要投资者的国籍已由美国当局正式记录，因此鉴于涉及的美国利益，美方准备向主要投资者提供全面的领事保护。相信当两位英国投资者在其领事馆正式注册后，他们也将获得英国领事馆的同等待遇保护。

该电台是作为商业 venture 建立的，主要负责人现在发现，严格遵守交通部的规章会危及电台在其常规广告商中的受欢迎程度，而电台的大部分收入来源于这些广告商。因此，他们不再遵守交通部的要求，交通部最近就电台的活动向美国领事提出了投诉。相信在此次事件中，美国当局已向中国当局清楚地表明了其立场。

one of the two writers of the attached letter, form the
standing committee with Mr. Wong Wan-pah(王完白) as Chairman.
The other signatory of the letter, Mr. Chow Pang-
tsing(周邦俊), is a member of the Shanghai Municipal Council
Advisory Committee for 1937, and is manager of the Great
China Dispensary, corner of Foochow and Shantung Roads,
and concurrently manager of the Great China Dispensary
Broadcasting Station, which is attached to the Dispensary.
He is a member of the Broadcasting Station Association.
Following the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities on
August 13, he was appointed by the Shanghai Various Circles
Committee to Support Resistance against the Enemy, as Officer
i/c of the Propaganda Section, which would account for his
signature appearing in the attached letter.
The object of this Association is to promote unity
among local Chinese broadcasting station owners, in order
to avoid unfair competition in the matter of fees for
advertisements. The association being registered with the
Kuomintang, its members are obliged to broadcast Government
propaganda and registration also gives control to the Chinese
authorities.
There are 26 stations members of this association

上述前五名人员，包括随信两位撰写人之一的 Soo Chu-kuo，组成常务委员会，由 Wong Wan-pah先生(王完白) 担任主席。
该信的另一位签署人 Chow Pang-tsing先生(周邦俊)，是1937年上海公共租界工部局华员顾问委员会成员，也是福州路与山东路转角的大中华药房经理，同时兼任附设于该药房的大中华药房广播电台经理。他是广播电台同业公会的成员。
自8月13日中日敌对行动爆发以来，他被上海各界抗敌后援会任命为宣传部主任，这解释了他的签名出现在随附信件中的原因。
该公会的宗旨是促进本地中国电台业主之间的团结，以避免在广告费方面的不公平竞争。由于该会在国民党注册，其成员有义务广播政府宣传内容，且注册也使中国当局拥有控制权。
该协会有26家电台会员

August 21, 1937.

Sirs,

we are glad that the Council has made
arrangements with the Great China and Hwa Shing
Broadcasting Stations relative to the broadcasting
of news. However, as no definite time is
scheduled for its broadcasting, it is difficult
to carry out the plan. We therefore request the
Council to fix time limits. Except from 8 p.m. to
9.05 p.m., when stations are required to relay the
programme of the Central Broadcasting Station, the
Council should choose any time and also arrange with
the Shanghai Municipality Broadcasting Association
that the Council broadcast from one station and the
programme then relayed by other stations. The
programmes for broadcasting should be sent to Tseu
Paung Tsing(周邦俊) or Soo Tsoo Kwoh(苏祖国), Chinese
Chamber of Commerce, "4th floor", Ningpo Fellow
Countrymen's Association, Yu Ya Ching Road.

Mention should be made of the fact that the Nanking
Station of the Central Kuomintang is easily tuned in by the
greater proportion of Chinese owned sets in Shanghai and the
news broadcast over this station may from time to time contain
misleading reports.
A representative of station XMHA (5) stated that
all news broadcast by the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury over
that station was done so by remote control, i.e. from the
offices of the newspaper, and that the station was unable to
check any news reports prior to its being broadcast. The
representative was informed that the station would be held
responsible for anything infringing the contents of the
Emergency Order.

EMERGENCY ORDER

In the present serious emergency nothing
can more easily cause alarm and panic than mis-
leading reports. All proprietors of wireless
stations are most earnestly urged in the public
interest to take immediate steps to ensure that no
reports are published unless confirmed by competent
authorities. Failure to comply with this request
must necessarily result in immediate closure of
the station concerned by the Police.

By Order

REPORT

S. 1. Special Branch /Station/. File No.................... Date September 23, 1941.

SUBJECT: Radio Station X.H.H.R. -
Complaint of interference

With reference to the attached letter from
C.M. Skepper, Manager, Raytone Broadcasting Company,
complaining of interference with the broadcasts over
Radio Station X.H.H.R., 517 Bubbling Well Road, I
have to report having interviewed the writer on
September 19th, 1941.

Mr. Skepper was informed that there is no
apparatus available to the Police whereby it would
be possible to trace the cause of the interference.

Radio Station X.H.H.R. (840 K.C.) is
registered with the Japanese Broadcasting
Superintendence Office as being owned by a Japanese,
Teiji Miyahara. The manager is understood to have
been a Chinese named Chang. On September 1st, 1941,
Mr. Skepper, on behalf of the British Press Attache,
purchased X.H.H.R. from Chang and on September 15th,
1941, the station went on the air with Chinese
programmes and news of a pro-British nature.

Since 5 p.m. 16th, September, 1941,
interference in the form of a high pitched hum has
been broadcast on the same wave-length as that of
X.H.H.R., completely distorting the programmes.

On 20th, September, 1941, Mr. Skepper received
a letter from the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence
Office pointing out that the sale of X.H.H.R. was
illegal as it is registered in the name of a Japanese,
Teiji Miyahara. Mr. Skepper was accordingly
"strongly requested" by the above office to cease

干扰投诉

关于附呈的雷通广播公司（Raytone Broadcasting Company）经理 C.M. Skepper 的来信，投诉位于静安寺路517号的 X.H.H.R. 电台广播受到干扰一事，本人谨报告已于1941年9月19日约谈了写信人。

已告知 Skepper 先生，警方没有可用的设备来追踪干扰源。

X.H.H.R. 电台（840千周）在日本放送监督局注册为日本人宫原贞二（Teiji Miyahara）所有。据悉，其经理是一名姓张的中国人。1941年9月1日，Skepper 先生代表英国新闻参赞从张某手中购买了 X.H.H.R. 电台，并于1941年9月15日开始播出中文节目及亲英性质的新闻。

自1941年9月16日下午5时起，在与 X.H.H.R. 相同的波长上广播了一种高音调的嗡嗡声形式的干扰，完全扭曲了节目内容。

1941年9月20日，Skepper 先生收到日本放送监督局的一封信，指出 X.H.H.R. 的出售是非法的，因为它注册在日本人宫原贞二名下。因此，上述部门“强烈要求” Skepper 先生停止

page_data.en:
At 11 a.m. on November 15th 1940 members of
the Japanese Gendarmerie accompanied to C.B.H.Q.
C.I. the complainant, Tan Pei Pei (戴倍佩)
aged 25, who reported that he had been the reci-
pient of two letters which threatened him bodily
harm if he failed to resign from his present
position.
Tan Pei Pei and his wife Tan Yue Sz (戴于氏)
reside in a room over the Dah Tseong Woo (大中華).
Cigar Factory situated at No.10 Lane 51 Tientsin
Road.
For the past two years he and his wife have
both been employed by the Greater Shanghai Radio
Broadcasting Co., offices Aster House Hotel
Whangpoo Road.
Daily, usually during the afternoon they broad-
cast in Chinese over radio station X.O.J.B. from
studios located at the Aster House and room No.320
Hudson Building, Nanking Road. The broadcasts
which they give comprise only the children's hour.
In addition to being employed by the Broadcast-
ing Co, to augment his earnings complainant gives
private violin lessons.
On 28-9-40 he received by post at his home the
following letter :-
To Tan Pei Pei and Tan Dai Sz,
It is learned that you both work for
the enemy and betray our country, acting
on instructions of the enemy...
page_data.zh:
1940年11月15日上午11时，日本宪兵队成员陪同投诉人戴倍佩（Tan Pei Pei），25岁，前往中央捕房刑侦总部。他报告说收到了两封信，威胁如果他不辞去目前的职位，将对他人身伤害。
戴倍佩及其妻子戴于氏（Tan Yue Sz）居住在天津路51弄10号大中华雪茄厂楼上的一个房间里。
过去两年里，他和妻子都受雇于大上海广播公司，办公地点位于黄浦路阿斯特豪斯酒店（Aster House Hotel）。
每天，通常在下午，他们通过位于阿斯特豪斯和南京路哈逊大楼320室的演播室，在 X.O.J.B. 电台用中文广播。他们的广播内容仅包括儿童时段节目。
除了在广播公司任职以增加收入外，投诉人还私下教授小提琴课。
1940年9月28日，他在家中通过邮局收到如下信件：-
致戴倍佩及戴代氏（Tan Dai Sz），
获悉你二人为敌人工作，背叛我国，听从敌人指令行事……

page_data.en:
√3

... press ... to both of you and
further you are ordered to resign your
wor ... from the enemy, otherwise to complete
our plan of killing traitors you will be in
danger. After seeing this letter you have to
explain in your manner in the Sun Wen Pao and
Sun Pao, two newspapers.
Hoping you will not delay our warning, or
you will be executed.

Chinese Kuomintang Youth
Party Local Headquarters.

This letter was posted at No.25 Sub Post
Office, Rme County.

He did not attach any importance to the letter
and did not mention the receipt of same to anyone.

On 12-11-40 he again received by post at his
home address, a copy of the Shun Pao newspaper, contained
in which was a further threatening letter and a .32
round of ammunition.

The second letter reads as follows :-

Traitor Tam Bui Pai,

You are still serving the enemy. Your noto-
rious guilt of betraying our country cannot be
described, therefore we are instructed by our
superior to give you this last warning i.e. you
page_data.zh:
√3

……向你们二人施压……
此外，命令你们辞去为敌人服务的职……务，否则为了完成我们诛杀汉奸的计划，你们将面临危险。见到此信后，你们必须在《孙文报》和《申报》两家报纸上以你们的方式作出解释。
希望你们不要延误我们的警告，否则将被处决。

中国国民党青年党
地方总部。

这封信是在崇明县第25支局寄出的。

他并未重视这封信，也未向任何人提及收到此信之事。

1940年11月12日，他再次在家中的地址通过邮局收到一份《申报》，其中包含另一封威胁信和一颗 .32 口径子弹。

第二封信内容如下：-

叛徒谭培派（Tam Bui Pai，音译，即戴倍佩），

你仍在为敌人服务。你背叛我国的臭名昭著的罪行难以形容，因此我们奉上级指示给你最后警告，即你

page_data.en:
1/4

must leave Shanghai within three days,
otherwise you get some bullets to eat.

Blue Shirts Traitor Exter-
mination 2nd Detachment.

The newspaper is dated 16.11.40 and was posted
at the B'Well post office. Upon receipt of this second
letter complainant reported to the Japanese Gendarmerie,
also he and his wife moved to the Aster House where
they have taken up temporary residence.

Complainant does not suspect any particular indi-
vidual and the reason he is being threatened is obvious.
Enquiries at the Dah Tseong Woo cigar factory have
failed to glean any useful information.

For the next few days complainant will remain in
the Hongkew Area and he has been instructed to report
to the Police immediately the receipt of any further
threats.

Special Branch,
May 21, 1940.

Steel tower to be erected in Pootung.
--------------------------------------

With reference to the attached extract
from the North China Daily News date May 20, 1940,
regarding the reported erection of a steel tower in
Pootung, I have to state that the report is correct.
The tower will be erected in Pootung opposite the
Chinese Maritime Customs by the "Toa Hoko Kai" or
the "East Asia Public Service Association" in Tokyo
for publicity purposes.

The steel tower will be 150 metres in
height, and will be built by Ishimoto Gumi, a
Japanese constructor, No. 383 Changchun Road, the
work to be completed in October of this year.

News items and advertisements in electric
lights will be used on the tower and will be in the
Chinese and English language.

In addition to the above tower, a smaller
one is projected for Yangtzepoo district, Chapei
and also the Western district, but plans are
indefinite for these projects.

The attached is the drawing of the
projected steel tower in Pootung.

Certified true copy

J. F. Lovell
ccp.

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

MAY 20 1940

Electric Pagodas to Be
Erected Here

To Broadcast in English
And Japanese

In order to "direct" the people liv-
ing in foreign areas here with "light"
and "sound", four "electric informa-
tion pagodas" will be erected in Poo-
tung and other Chinese areas in
Shanghai by the Japanese for pub-
licity purposes, according to the "Sin
Shun Pao." These pagodas, it is
learned, will be high, illuminated
broadcasting stations, one of which
will stand on the shore on the Poo-
tung side of the Whangpoo just op-
posite the Customs building on the
Bund.

Construction of these steel towers
which will shoot 150 feet high into
the sky is being planned by a Japan-
ese company and work will be started
in the near future. Hope is express-
ed that the Pootung "pagoda" will be
ready for use in four months when
information in both Chinese and
English will be broadcast.

It is being planned that in addition
to the Pootung station, three other
stations will be erected in Hongkew,
Chapei and the western district.
The Hongkew one will be built near
a fruit hong.

据悉，这些宝塔将是高耸的、带有照明设备的
广播电台，其中一座将矗立在黄浦江浦东一侧
的岸边，正对外滩的海关大楼。

这些将射向天空150英尺高的钢塔的
建设正由一家日本公司规划，工程将于
近期开工。人们表示希望浦东的“宝塔”
能在四个月内投入使用，届时将广播
中文和英文信息。

据计划，除浦东站外，还将在虹口、
闸北和西区 erect 另外三个站点。

CHENJU STATION TO
BROADCAST AGAIN
Four New 20-Kilowatt
Transmitters To Be
Installed Soon

TOKYO, Feb. 20 —Broadcasts will soon be resumed by the radio station at Chenju, suburb of Shanghai, when transmission to points in Europe, including Berlin, will be started on February 21.

The Chenju station was completely destroyed by Japanese land and air attacks early in the hostilities.

Preparations for resuming broadcasts have been steadily progressing at the hands of the Central China Electric Communications Company, subsidiary of the Central China Development Company.

A series of test broadcasts recently with points in North China as well as Osaka, Hongkong, and Manila proved successful. Four 20-kilowatt transmitters will be added to the radio station by July this year, according to reports.—Domei.

February 1, 1939.

Newly established Japanese Broadcasting Station
will adopt same wavelength as Dah Chung Hwa
Station, French Concession
--------------------------------------------------

The attached letter dated January 26, 1939 from Major
Kazuo Asano, Superintendent, Broadcasting Superintendence
Office, was passed to Special Branch by D.C. (Japanese).

It will be seen from the contents that Major Asano has
issued a permit to establish a new radio broadcasting station
to a Japanese subject, namely Teiji Miyahara. The station
which will be known as Lai Tung Radio Station, will be located
at 15 Love Lane. Call sign - X.H.H.R. wavelength frequency
- K.C. 840, power - 100 watts. The wavelength frequency
allocated by Major Asano to this station is the same as that
over which the Dah Chung Hwa Station (XHHU), French Concession,
has been and in fact, still is broadcasting.

It would appear, therefore, that the Japanese, despite
their repeated assurances to respect the rights of established
stations, are determined to suppress all stations not register-
ed with the Broadcasting Superintendence Office. The informa-
tion contained in Major Asano's letter has been passed to the
French Police.

Certified true copy
H. C. Eardley
EFT/.

从内容可见，浅野少校已向一名日本臣民，

因此，尽管日本人一再保证尊重既有电台的权利，

The wavelength frequency allocated by Major Asano to this
station is the same as that over which the Dr. Chung Hwa
Station (XHU), French Concession, has been and in fact,
still is broadcasting.
It would appear, therefore, that the Japanese,
despite their repeated assurances to respect the rights
of established stations, are determined to suppress all
stations not registered with the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office. The information contained in Major Asano's letter
has been passed to the French Police.

Shanghai, January 20, 1939.
Registered
To the Commissioner of Police Force,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
185 Fouchow Road,
Shanghai.

Sir,

Acting under instructions of Mr. Charles Mader, I
have the honour to approach you on the following subject :-

My client is a sole proprietor and owner of the Radio
Station under the name of "X H H G Radio Broadcast Station",
731 Canton Road (120 Yu Ya Ching Road) as per a Bill of Sale
dated December 2nd, 1938, and duly registered at H.B.M.
Consulate-General at Shanghai on the 12th of December, 1938,
under No.607. A copy of said Bill of Sale has been duly
deposited by me at the Office of the Headquarters of the
Shanghai Municipal Police. The said Radio Station is operating
on K.C. 1220. But some time ago it was established by my
client that some other Radio Station is using the same
kilocycle causing thereby harm and confusion to interests of
my client. As a certain Mei Sung Radio Station, 432 Nanking
Road, announced in Chinese Press some time ago that it will
use said kilocycle my client suspects that the Radio Station
in question is said Mei Sung Radio Station.

Under those circumstances I have the honour to
request you to investigate the matter and to take necessary
steps in order to stop, if it is possible, such activity in
future or to let me know the name and address of the Radio
Station using the same kilocycle as the Radio Station of my
client (1220 K.C.) and who is a registered owner of said
Radio Station.

Awaiting your prompt answer.

I have the honour to be,

Sir,

Your obedient servant,

N.A. Ivanow.

先生，

受 Charles Mader 先生指示，我就以下事项荣幸地与您联系：-

我的客户是名为“X H H G 无线电广播电台”的电台的唯一 proprietor 和业主，地址为广东路731号（虞洽卿路120号），依据1938年12月2日的卖契，并于1938年12月12日在上海英国总领事馆正式注册，编号607。该卖契副本已由我正式存置于上海公共租界工部局警务处总部办公室。该电台正在 K.C. 1220 频率上运营。但不久前，我的客户查明有其他广播电台使用相同的千周率，从而损害了我的客户的利益并造成混乱。由于某美声广播电台（南京路432号）不久前在中文报刊上宣布将使用所述千周率，我的客户怀疑涉事电台即为该美声广播电台。

在此情况下，我荣幸地请求您调查此事，并采取必要措施，以便在可能的情况下阻止此类活动在未来发生，或告知使用与我客户电台相同千周率（1220 K.C.）的广播电台的名称和地址，以及该电台的注册业主是谁。

期待您的迅速回复。

我荣幸地成为，

先生，

您顺从的仆人，

N.A. Ivanow。

Date January 23, 19 39
Subject Mei Sung Broadcasting Station (XQMS) K.C.1220 established.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C Crawford S. I.

With reference to the attached letter dated
January 19, 1939, from Major Asano, Japanese broadcasting
Superintendence Office and the letter dated January 19,
1939, from Mr. Y. Ikeda (Japanese), 453 Dixwell Road,
announcing that a new broadcasting Station to be known as
"Mei Sung" (美声) call sign XQMS, wavelength K.C.1220,
power 100 watts, of which Mr. Ikeda is the owner, has been
established at 423 Nanking Road, it should be noted that
Major Asano is in error when he states in his letter
that the "frequency of K.C.1220 formerly used by the Tong
Fong Radio Station has been allotted to the Mei Sung Station"
inasmuch as the Tung Fong Station continues to use K.C.1220.
This is another instance of the Japanese interfering with
the rights of an established station for no other reason
than that the owner has refused to yield to the efforts of
the Japanese to obtain control.

Mr. Creighton, H.B.M. Consulate-General, has been
informed of the contents of Major Asano's letter.

Mr. Charles Nadar, 259 Kiangse Road, was informed
of the contents of Major Asano's letter on January 23, 1939
and in reply stated that he was placing the matter in the
hands of Mr. A.A. Ivanow, Attorney and Counsellor-at-Law.

Logan
D. S. I.

D.S. (Special Branch)

January 19, 1939.

Police Department,
S. M. C.

Re Permit Granted To Mei Sung Radio Station

Dear Sirs,

In pursuance of our policy of suppressing
all unregistered radio stations within the territory
under the jurisdiction of this office as contained in
our letter addressed to you on 30th November 1938, we
have to inform you that the carrier frequency of 1,220
k.c., formerly used by the Tong Fong Radio Station, has
been allotted to the Mei Sung Radio Station(美聲電台)
which is Japanese owned. The installation of this
station having passed our test, the Mei Sung Radio
Station was granted permission to operate as from
to-day. The following is the particulars of this station:
Name .................... Mei Sung Radio Station
Licensee ................ Mr. Yasuzo IKEDA
Address ................. 423 Nanking Road, Shanghai.
Call signal ............. X Q M S.
Carrier frequency ....... 1,220 k.c.
Power ................... 100 w.

Incidentally, it has come to our notice recently that
the management of the Tong Fong Radio Station has published
an advertisement in one of the local vernaculars to the
effect that this station has been sold to a British
concern named "MaTei Yang Hung"(麥度洋行). In this
connection, we have to point out that it is our determination
to eliminate all unauthorized radio station in this area,
irrespective of the nationality of the licensee, and in the case
of the Tong Fong Radio Station, too, drastic steps, in the
form of wave disturbance, will be taken by us to compel the
said station to cease operations.

敬启者：

根据我们在1938年11月30日致贵处的信函中所述，在本处管辖区域内取缔所有未注册广播电台的政策，我们特此通知，原由通丰广播电台使用的1,220 k.c.载波频率已分配给日资拥有的美声广播电台（美聲電台）。该台安装已通过我方测试，美声广播电台获准自今日起运营。该电台详情如下：

呼号 ............. X Q M S.
载波频率 ....... 1,220 k.c.
功率 ................... 100 w.

顺便提一下，我们最近注意到，通丰广播电台管理层在一种本地 vernaculars 报纸上刊登广告，称该电台已出售给一家名为“麦度洋行”（MaTei Yang Hung）的英国商行。对此，我们必须指出，我们决心消除该地区所有未经授权的广播电台，无论持证人的国籍如何，对于通丰广播电台，我们也将在波形干扰方面采取严厉措施，迫使该台停止运营。

X.Q.M.S. to adopt same frequency as that of Tung Fang Station.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C Crawford.

On December 6, 1938, an advertisement to the
following effect appeared in the Sin Wan Pao Evening
Edition :-
"Mei Sung (美聲) Broadcasting Station, call
sign XQMS, K.C.1220, will commence broadcasting
soon. Address: 1st floor, Hwa Hwa Hosiery Shop,
423 Nanking Road. Tel.93414."

It is to be noted that the frequency to be adopted by this
station, i.e. K.C.1220, has already been adopted by the
Tung Fang Station, 120 Yu Ya Ching Road, which is not
registered with the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence
Office. It will be remembered that the Tung Fang Station
originally operated on a frequency of K.C.1080, and changed
to the present frequency, K.C.1220, in July, 1938, in
consequence of the allocation of the former frequency by
the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office to a new
station, namely, Yung Sung (永生) call sign XHHJ. At
the time in question, Mr. Uyehara, D.C. (Japanese) was
informed of the change and in turn informed Major Asano,
who, stated that he had no objection (vide remarks of D.C.
(Japanese) on memo. dated 26/7/38 by D.C. (Special Branch)).

Enquiries made at the Hwa Hwa Hosiery Shop show
that the lease of the premises by the proposed Mei Sung
Station, which was taken by one named Chang (張) (address
unknown), will take effect from December 15, 1938.
Installation of the station equipment has not yet been

Subject Japanese owned Dah Tung radio station (X.Q.H.A.) K.C.660
obtruding on (X.M.H.A.) K.C.600 (American owned).

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.I.

I beg to report that between 7 p.m., and 7.30 p.m.,
on 24-10-38, I listened in to a programme of waltzes broad-
cast from the Japanese owned radio broadcasting station known
as Dah Tung ( 大東 ) located on Whangpoo Wharf (X.Q.H.A.,
K.C.660) on the radio set in my home at Flat 216, House 2,
Majestic Apartments. At the termination of the programme
of waltzes, the female announcer announced that a programme,
relayed from Japan, would be broadcast over the Station.
I waited until the programme commenced and upon noting that it
was in Japanese, switched to the American owned station known
as X.M.H.A. located at 445 Racecourse Road (K.C.600) but
found that the Japanese broadcast from K.C.660 was obtruding
on K.C.600 and completely blocking out the broadcast from the
latter station. After attempting, unsuccessfully, to
eliminate the interference for a period of a few minutes, I
abandoned the attempt and did not again use the radio on the
date mentioned.

My radio set is a 5 tube R.C.A. Victor and the
instance mentioned above is the only one where any interference
with X.M.H.A., K.C.600, broadcasts has been noted.

The Dah Tung Station is not registered with the
S.M.P. and there is nothing on record concerning it.

Logan
D. S. I.

DOYLE
D.C. (Special Branch)

Copy sent to
Mr. Dyechan

呈报人 副督察长洛根 转呈人 C. 克劳福德 副督察长。

谨此报告，1938年10月24日晚7时至7时30分间，我在位于玛杰司蒂克公寓（Majestic Apartments）2号楼216室的家中收音机上，收听了位于黄浦码头（Whangpoo Wharf）的日资广播电台大东（Dah Tung）（呼号 X.Q.H.A.，千周660）播放的华尔兹舞曲节目。华尔兹舞曲节目结束后，女播音员宣布，该台将转播来自日本的节目。我等待至节目开始，发现是日语广播后，便切换至位于跑马厅路445号的美资电台 X.M.H.A.（千周600），但发现来自千周660的日本广播干扰了千周600，完全掩盖了后者的广播。在尝试了几分钟未能消除干扰后，我放弃了尝试，并在上述日期未再使用收音机。

我的收音机是一台5管 RCA Victor 牌，上述情况是唯一一次注意到对 X.M.H.A. 千周600 广播产生干扰的情况。

大东电台未在上海公共租界工部局警务处注册，档案中亦无相关记录。

Japanese Club, Boone Road, where for some time the Station

The Great Shanghai Broadcasting Station, call

Kindergarten school owned by the Shanghai Cotton
Spinning and Weaving Company, Ningkuo Road near

anti-Nationalist Government and anti-Communist propaganda
and on one occasion was heard broadcasting anti-British
propaganda (vide Special Branch report dated 4/6/38).
Broadcasts are chiefly in the Chinese language but
sometimes English and Japanese is spoken.

The Greater Shanghai Radio Broadcasting Station,
call letters X.O.J.B., frequency K.C. 900, was established
by the Japanese Military Authorities in Shanghai to meet
the requirements of their military operations, in the
kindergarten school owned by the Shanghai Cotton Spinning
and Weaving Company situated on Ningkuo Road near
Pingliang Road towards the beginning of November, 1937.
The main office of this radio station later was removed
to the Japanese Club, Boone Road, while an auxiliary
broadcasting station was established in Room 220-222,
Hardoon Building, 233 Nanking Road.

Military Authorities established the Radio Broadcasting
Superintendence Office in the Hardoon Building with Major
K. Asano, officer in charge of the Radio Broadcasting

chief of the Greater Shanghai Radio Broadcasting Station.

page_data.en:
A SERIOUS DISABILITY

SHANGHAI has been seriously disabled in the way of communications. With the closure of the Chinese telegraph office and the radio station, this city is virtually cut off from the rest of China. The situation is not a little tragic when it is remembered that Shanghai, as represented by the International Settlement and French Concession, can hardly be regarded as under military occupation, and yet the situation is probably an inevitable outcome of the peculiar status of the foreign administrative areas.

It is generally admitted that both the Settlement and the Concession are entitled to the rights ordinarily accorded to a neutral territory. Within their confines the nationals and official organs of either belligerent should be free to conduct legitimate trade without molestation and hindrance, provided that no act is performed by those of one which is likely to prejudice the rights of the other. The observance of this elementary rule of international comity is most essential if Shanghai is still to retain its importance as the sixth largest port of the world.

Thus, while hostilities were conducted around Shanghai, the Chinese Mayor of Greater Shanghai and the Japanese Ambassador to China were both offered haven in the French Concession. Though Mayor O. K. Yui has left the French Concession since the withdrawal of Chinese forces to the interior, presumably his right to reside therein is not thereby waived or impaired, provided of course that he would confine his activities to those of a non-military character.

The Chinese telegraph office, however, may belong to a slightly different category. On the one hand it is a commercial enterprise, in that it caters to the mercantile community without distinction, and on the other it is doubtless an important organ to the Chinese Government, in that its services are essential to the transmission of military or quasi-military information when other means are no longer available. It is, therefore, not difficult to understand the desire of the Japanese to control its administration, so that their rights as a belligerent may not in consequence be impaired. At the same time, as the office is primarily a Chinese government organ, it is only natural that its employees loyal to the Chinese Government should refuse to submit to Japanese control.

The impasse thus created will not yield to solution through direct negotiation between the Chinese and Japanese authorities. Yet unless this impasse is overcome, Shanghai must suffer from a serious disability in its network of communication facilities.

From certain quarters it has been proposed that an international committee be formed to maintain this essential service in the interim. This modus vivendi is expected to assure the Japanese of the use of the service strictly for commercial purposes and to preserve its Chinese legal status.

While legal opinion may not all agree in an academic sense, the proposal appears to us to be the most practical one in the circumstances. Once this proposal is accepted by both sides concerned, the details of organisation will probably present no insurmountable difficulties. The urgency of the paramount need for communication facilities should be able to impress itself upon all Shanghai citizens, and no time should be lost to bring about a solution which will redound to the interest not of any one particularly national group but to all national groups.
page_data.zh:
严重的功能障碍

上海在通讯方面已遭受严重障碍。随着中国电报局和无线电台的关闭，这座城市实际上已与中国的其他地区隔绝。鉴于上海（以国际租界和法租界为代表）很难被视为处于军事占领之下，而目前的局势又可能是外国行政区域特殊地位的必然结果，这一局面不免令人感到有些悲惨。

人们普遍承认，租界和法租界均有权享有通常赋予中立领土的权利。在其范围内，任何交战国的国民和官方机构应可自由进行合法贸易，不受干扰和阻碍，前提是其中一方的行为不得有可能损害另一方的权利。如果上海仍要保持其作为世界第六大港口的重要性，遵守这一基本的国际礼让规则至关重要。

因此，尽管战事在上海周边进行，但上海特别市市长俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui）和日本驻中国大使均在法租界获得了庇护。虽然随着中国军队撤往内地，俞市长已离开法租界，但只要他将活动限制在非军事性质范围内，推测其居住权并未因此被放弃或受损。

然而，中国电报局可能属于稍有不同的类别。一方面，它是一家商业企业，不分彼此地为商界提供服务；另一方面，它无疑是中国政府的重要机构，因为当其他手段不再可用时，其服务对于传递军事或准军事信息至关重要。因此，不难理解日本希望控制其管理，以免其作为交战国的权利因此受到损害。同时，由于该局主要是一个中国政府机构，忠于中国政府的雇员拒绝服从日本控制也是自然之事。

由此造成的僵局无法通过中日当局之间的直接谈判来解决。然而，除非克服这一僵局，上海必须在通讯设施网络方面遭受严重的功能障碍。

有方面提议成立一个国际委员会，在此期间维持这项基本服务。这种临时安排预计将向日本保证该服务仅用于商业目的，并保留其中方合法地位。

虽然在学术意义上法律意见可能不尽一致，但在当前情况下，该提议对我们来说似乎是最切实可行的。一旦有关双方接受这一提议，组织细节方面可能不会出现不可逾越的困难。对通讯设施的迫切需求这一首要需要应当能让所有上海市民印象深刻，不应浪费时间，以促成一项不仅有利于任何一个特定民族群体，而且有利于所有民族群体的解决方案。

December 1, 1937. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

EFFORTS BEING MADE TO RESUME TELEGRAPHIC COMMUNICATIONS

As all the telegraph offices of the Ministry of Communications in Shanghai were taken over by the Japanese authorities on November 28, telegraphic communications between this city and other parts of China have been interrupted. The Great Northern, the Great Eastern and the Pacific Telegraph Companies are only accepting telegrams to Kwangsi and Kwangtung to be delivered via Hongkong and the charges have been considerably increased. This is causing much inconvenience to Chinese and foreign merchants.

It is now learned that the telegraph offices are making arrangements to restore the telegraph service. Foreign merchants are also discussing the situation. It is hoped to restore the telegraph service between this city and outports at an early date.

After taking over the Chinese Telegraph Administration, deputies of the Japanese authorities remained in the office. On November 30, the deputies removed two machines from the Telegraph Administration on Bubbling Well Road. It is said that the British policemen stationed there attempted to stop them from removing the machines, but without success.

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

RICE SITUATION EASIER: RESTAURANTS RE-OPENING

The fourth consignment of Saigon rice, comprising 30,000 bags, bought by the Shanghai Municipal Council and the South China Rice Company through Dreyfus & Co., will arrive in Shanghai on the s.s. Chekiang on December 3.

The French liner Jean Laborde arrived yesterday morning with 500 tons (about 5,000 bags) of Saigon rice bought by Dreyfus & Co. on behalf of local factories and benevolent organizations. The usual custom duties were paid.

With the assistance of the authorities of the International Settlement and the French Concession, local rice dealers are buying large quantities of rice from Annam through British and French merchants. It is estimated that 150,000 bags of rice will arrive between December 2 and 15.

The rice dealers are also buying 300,000 piculs of Chinese rice from Wenchow, Taichow and Ningpo. Certificates have been issued by the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce and the rice will be shipped to Shanghai by ships of Butterfield & Swire and of the China Navigation Co. The first consignment will arrive on December 10.

Negotiations for the release of 20,000 piculs of Chinese rice from Nantao have so far met with little success.

Fifteen new rice shops have been opened in the International Settlement after obtaining licences through the Chamber of Commerce.

Owing to the arrival of large quantities of Saigon rice, most of the restaurants have resumed business.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

正努力恢复电报通讯

由于交通部在上海的所有电报局于11月28日被日本当局接管，本市与中国其他地区的电报通讯已中断。大北电报公司、大东电报公司和太平洋电报公司仅接收发往广西和广东的电报，经由香港投递，且费用已大幅增加。这给中外商人带来了诸多不便。

现获悉，各电报局正在安排恢复电报服务。外商也在讨论这一局势。希望能早日恢复本市与外埠之间的电报服务。

接管中国电信管理局后，日本当局的代表留在办公室内。11月30日，代表们从静安寺路的电信管理局移走了两台机器。据说驻扎在那里的英国警察曾试图阻止他们移走机器，但未成功。

大米局势缓和：餐馆重新开业

由上海公共租界工部局和华南米业公司通过 Dreyfus & Co. 购买的第四批西贡大米，共计30,000袋，将于12月3日由“浙江”轮（s.s. Chekiang）运抵上海。

法国邮轮“让·拉博德”号（Jean Laborde）于昨晨抵达，载有500吨（约5,000袋）西贡大米，系 Dreyfus & Co. 代表本地工厂和慈善组织购买。已缴纳常规关税。

在国际租界和法租界当局的协助下，本地米商正通过英法商人从安南大量购买大米。估计在12月2日至15日期间将有150,000袋大米运抵。

米商还从温州、台州和宁波购买300,000担中国大米。上海总商会已签发证书，大米将由太古轮船公司（Butterfield & Swire）和中国航运公司（China Navigation Co.）的船只运往上海。第一批货物将于12月10日抵达。

关于释放南市20,000担中国大米的谈判迄今收效甚微。

通过总商会获得执照后，国际租界内新开设了十五家米店。

由于大量西贡大米运抵，大多数餐馆已恢复营业。

page_data.en:
Japanese To Take Over
Post Office, Telegraph
And Radio This Morning

JAPANESE APPRAISERS AND EXAMINERS
WILL BE ASSIGNED FOR DUTY ON
BUND AS WELL AS FRENCH BUND

CITY GOVERNMENT PONTOON OCCUPIED;
MAY SEIZE CUSTOMS JETTY

Issue Not Clear Whether Jardine Matheson Will Be
Allowed To Land Cargo At City Government
Pontoon; Application Will Be Studied

Japanese authorities will this morning assume control over
the Chinese Government's communications facilities in Shanghai,
Domei learnt last night from authoritative sources.
Taken over will be the Post Office, the Telegraph Office, the
Chinese Government's Radio Administration and radio station
XOHC, owned and operated by the Ministry of Communications.
Indicating further extension of Japanese influence, Japanese
appraisers and examiners of the Maritime Customs will be
assigned for duty on The Bund and the French Bund, Domei
was informed.

This will follow close on the heels
of the appointment of two Japanese,
Mr. Yoshisuke Akatani and Mr.
Keiichi Kato, as Administrative
Commissioner and Revenue Ac-
countant respectively in the local
Customs office.

Pontoon Occupied

The City Government's pontoon on
Peking Road was occupied by Jap-
anese troops yesterday afternoon.
The s.s. Fooshing, of Messrs. Jardine,
Matheson and Company was at the
time berthed at the pontoon.

Owned by the City Government
of Greater Shanghai, the floating
restaurant, which had before the
outbreak of hostilities been a popular
tiffin rendezvous for city Chinese
business men, had lately been used
as a pontoon for the landing of
cargo by Messrs. Jardine Matheson.

The Japanese immediately sealed
the floating restaurant and all the
ticket offices and left a number of
soldiers on guard. The unloading
of rice from the s.s. Fooshing was
carried on, but the coolies had to
carry the bags around the south side
of the Floating Jetty, instead of
passing through it as previously.

Questioned later in the day on
whether the British concern will be
allowed to land cargo on the pon-
toon, a spokesman of the Japanese
Embassy said that was "another
question" from the seizure of the
pontoon.

If the firm makes an application
for permission to use the pontoon,
"it will be studied." No such ap-
plication has yet been received, the
spokesman said.

The Japanese authorities, the offi-
cial asserted, were justified in cap-
turing the ferry, since it was the
property of the Chinese Government.

Customs Jetty

"If necessity arose," the spokes-
man added, the Customs jetty, Han-
kow Road, might also be seized.

It could not be ascertained last
night whether or not Messrs. Jar-
dine, Matheson had permission from
the former City Government to use
the pontoon.

Ferry Service

Free ferry service between Way-
side and Pootung has been maintain-
ed since November 11, the Shang-
hai "United News" reported last
night.

Manned by 17 soldiers, the ferries
have been operating between the
Wayside Wharf and the Osaka
Shosen Kaisha's wharf on the other
side of the river.

This little force, the daily said, is
under the command of Engineer
Lieutenant Yasunao Kioka, who dis-
tinguished himself late in August,
when Japanese troops were landed
at Woosung, and later, at the battle
of Dazang.

Open to members of the armed
forces, as well as to civilians, this
service is temporary, but an applica-
tion has been made to the military
authorities for its continuation, the
daily reported.

日军今晨将接管

及广播电台

日本估价员与查验员
将在外滩及法租界外滩
执行职务

市政府趸船被占；
可能没收海关码头

怡和洋行是否获准在
市政府趸船卸货尚不明确；
申请将予研究

据同盟社昨晚从权威消息来源获悉，日本当局将于今晨接管中国政府在上海的通讯设施。将被接管的设施包括邮局、电报局、中国政府无线电管理处以及由交通部拥有并运营的XOHC广播电台。据告知同盟社，日本海关估价员和查验员将被派往外滩及法租界外滩执勤，这表明日本影响力的进一步扩大。

此举紧随两名日本人——赤谷义助（Yoshisuke Akatani，音译）先生和加藤庆一（Keiichi Kato，音译）先生——分别被任命为当地海关办公室的行政委员和税务会计师之后。

趸船被占

昨日下午，日军占领了位于北京路的市政府趸船。当时，怡和洋行（Messrs. Jardine, Matheson and Company）的“福兴”号轮船（s.s. Fooshing）正停靠在趸船旁。

这艘浮动餐厅归大上海市政府所有，在战事爆发前曾是上海中国商界人士喜爱的午餐聚会场所，最近被怡和洋行用作卸货趸船。

日军立即查封了该浮动餐厅及所有售票处，并留下数名士兵守卫。“福兴”号的卸米工作仍在进行，但苦力们不得不绕到浮动码头的南侧搬运米袋，而不能像以前那样直接穿过码头。

当日稍晚时候，当被问及这家英国公司是否被允许在趸船上卸货时，日本大使馆发言人称，这与没收趸船是“另一个问题”。

如果该公司提出使用趸船的申请，“将予以研究”。发言人表示，目前尚未收到此类申请。

该官员声称，日本当局扣押该渡轮是正当的，因为它是属于中国政府的财产。

海关码头

发言人补充说：“如果有必要”，位于汉口路的海关码头也可能被没收。

昨晚无法查明怡和洋行是否曾获得前任市政府使用趸船的许可。

渡轮服务

据《上海联合新闻》（Shanghai "United News"）昨晚报道，自11月11日以来，一直维持着从韦赛德（Wayside，音译）到浦东的免费渡轮服务。

渡轮由17名士兵操作，在韦赛德码头与河对岸的大阪商船会社（Osaka Shosen Kaisha）码头之间运营。

该日报称，这支小部队由木冈康直（Yasunao Kioka，音译）工兵中尉指挥，他在八月下旬日军登陆吴淞以及随后的大场战役中表现突出。

该日报报道，这项服务暂时向武装部队成员及平民开放，但已向军事当局申请继续维持此项服务。

Date Nov. 26, 1937.
Subject Central Government Radio Stations in the Settlement.
Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by
With reference to the queries of the D.C. (Special
Branch) appended to a report dated November 25, 1937, I
have to state that the radio station operated by the Chinese
Government Radio Administration at Sassoon House, Nanking
Road, is used to maintain an international service which
deals only in traffic of a commercial nature. Messages
are transmitted to and received from the stations of
various nations which, up to the time of forwarding this
report, include those of Japan. The report that the
C.G.R.A. has been taken over by the Radio Corporation of
America is not strictly correct. In July of this year
officials of R.C.A. signed an agreement with the Ministry
of Communications whereby the administration of the
C.G.R.A. passed into the hands of the American Corporation.
Nominal control, however, remained and still remains with
the Central Government.
It is of interest to note that the R.C.A. are
at the moment conducting negotiations with the Chinese
Director of Radio and Telegraph Communication, for the
transfer complete of C.G.R.A. If this transfer, which
will mean both nominal and virtual control of C.G.R.A.
by R.C.A., takes effect, an attempt will be made to effect
a transfer of the Chinese Telegraph Administration to
American control.
The Chinese Telegraph Administration which operates
from 70 Foochow Road and from 149-151/591 Bubbling Well
Road, apart from station X Q H C in Sassoon House, is
interested only in messages of a domestic, as distinct
from international nature. Transmission and reception,

日期：1937年11月26日。
主题：租界内的中央政府广播电台。
制作人：D.S. Henchman 转呈人：

关于附在1937年11月25日报告后的特别支部副主任（D.C.）的查询，我必须说明，由中国政府无线电管理处在南京路沙逊大厦运营的广播电台，用于维持一项仅处理商业性质业务的国际服务。电报发送至各国电台并从其接收，截至本报告转呈之时，其中包括日本的电台。关于中国政府无线电管理处已被美国无线电公司（R.C.A.）接管的说法并不完全准确。今年七月，美国无线电公司的官员与交通部签署了一项协议，据此，中国政府无线电管理处的行政管理权移交给这家美国公司。然而，名义上的控制权过去和现在仍保留在中央政府手中。

值得注意的是，美国无线电公司目前正与中国无线电报通信总监进行谈判，以求完全移交中国政府无线电管理处。如果这一移交生效，意味着美国无线电公司将同时获得对中国政府无线电管理处的名义和实际控制权，则将尝试把中国电信局也移交给美方控制。

除沙逊大厦的X Q H C电台外，从福州路70号和静安寺路149-151/591号运营的中国电信局，仅关注国内性质的电报，而非国际性质的电报。发送和接收，

REPORT
Date March 29, 1938.
Subject (in full) Dah Mei Radio Supply Company to commence functioning.
Made by C.D... Sin See Liang Forwarded by C Crawford I.S.

On March 28, 1938, Mr. I.D. Mai, manager of the Dah Mei
Radio Supply Company, 15 Fuboling Well Road, called at Police
Headquarters with the information that his Radio Station would
commence functioning as from April 1, 1938. At the same time
he submitted a copy of the programme (in Chinese), attached
hereto, which will be adopted by the Radio Station between
April 1 and April 4, inclusive. The programme contains sub-
jects, such as drama, songs and story-telling of the usual
nature and times of broadcast.

Mr. Mai was reminded that the introduction of anything
relating to politics or articles objectionable to the police
would entail immediate action, which instructions he stated
fully understood.

The wave length of this new station has been changed
from 1100 to 1140 kilocycles.

Sih See Liang
C. D. I.

Translation of letter received from Dah Mei Radio Supply Co.
15 Bubbling Well Road, on March 1,1938.
------------
Officer in Charge Special Branch.
This morning when Mr. Mei, manager of our
company, called on you in connection with the proposed
establishment of a broadcasting station, he received your
kind advice for which we wish to thank you. Arrangements
are still in progress and as soon as these are completed,
a formal notification will be sent to you. The broadcasting
station will be established purely for commercial purposes
and will observe the following conditions:-
1. The station will not broadcast any political programme
nor any programme or news objected to by the police.
2. All programmes before being used will be submitted to
the police for censorship.
3. The station will apply for registration if and when
the Radio Station Control Office is established in Shanghai.
4. All businesses transacted by the station will be in
accordance with police regulations.

Police Station, Chengtu Road Branch,
Present.

Sir,

As we are compelled to stop our business and most of the machines for radio-communication purposes have once more been taken away from our Wireless Division at No.149-161, Lane 591 on Bubbling Well Road by the Japanese, it is hard for us at present to work for the public.

We now decide to remove the remaining articles and furnitures from the above premises, and vacate the house so as to save unessential expenses. Mr. K.Y. Tseng, our engineer, is appointed to take charge of the removal, together with several coolies of this Office. It takes about one week to complete the work commencing to-day.

Besides writing to S.M.C. attached with a specified list of the machines, etc., which are taken away by the Japanese, we now write you in the hope that you will instruct your men to take necessary steps for the protection of the removal.

THE JAPANSSE RADIO STATION XQHA 


There is in Shanghai a Japanese radio 
broadcasting station whose calling signal is XQHA. 
According to newspaper reports, the programme of this 
radio station is frequently interrupted by a strange wave 

length. 

According to the Director of the Shanghai 
felegraph Administration, this Japanese radio station has 
no right to use its calling signal and wave length, nor 
has it the right to operate as a radio braatcasting station, 
because the management of this station, before it was 
bought over by Japanese from the American owners, had 
failed to secure the approval of the Ministry of 
Communications. Following the illegal transfer of this 
station to Japanese ownership, the Ministry of Communications 
has withdrawn its calling signal and wave length. It is 
learned that any legitimate radio station may now apply 
to the Ministry of Communications for the use of the letters 
XQHA as a calling signal and wave length No. 580.

A SERIOUS DISABILITY 


HANGHAL has been seriously disabled in the way of com- 
munications. With the closure of the Chinese telegraph 
office and the radio station, this city is virtually cut off fro 
the rest of China. The situation is not a Tithe tragic when 
iC is remembered that Shanghai, as represented by the In- 
ternational Settlement and French Concession, can hardly be 
regarded as under military occupation, and yet the situation | 
tspropably an inevitable outcome of tne peculiar status of | 
ihe foreign administrative areas. : 

It is generally admitted that both the Settlement and 
the Concession are entitled to the righis ordinarily accorde 
to a neutral territory. ithin thelr confines the nationals and 
WMclal VrYpans or either belligerent should be free to conduct 
legitimate trade without molestation and hindrance, provided 
that no act is performed b ich i ; 
préjudice s of t . The observance of er 
elementary ru international comity is most essential if 
Shanghai is still to retain its importance as the sixth largest 
port of the world. 

Thus, while hostilities were conducted around Shanghui. 
the Chinese Mayor of Greater Shanghai and the Japanese 
Ambassador to China were both offered hayen in the French 
Concession. Though Mayor O. K. Yui has left the French 
Concession since the withdrawal of Chinese forces to the in- 
terior, presumably his right to reside therein is not thereby 
waived or impaired, provided of course that he would confine 
his activities to those of a non-military character. 

The Chinese telegraph office, however, may belong to a 
slightly different category. On the one hand it is a com- 
mercial enterprise, in that it caters to the mercantile com-! 


at its ser-

The impasse thus created will not yield to solution 
through direct negotiation between the Chinese and Japanese 
authorities. Yet unless this impasse is overcome, Shanghai 
must suffer from a serious disability in its network of com- 
munication facilities. _ 7 id 
~~~"From certain quarters jt has been proposed that an in- 
ternational committee be formed to maintain this essential 
service in the interim. This modus vivendi is expected to 
assure the Japanese of the use of the service strictly for 
commercial purposes and to preserve its Chinese legal! status. 

While legal opinion may not all agree in an academic 


sense, the proposal appears to us to be the most practical 


one in the circumstances. Once this proposal is accepted by 
both sides concerned, the details of organisation will pro- 
hably present no insurmountable difficulties. The urgency 
of the paramount need for communication facilities should 
be able to impress itself upon al] Shanghai citizens, and no 
time should be lost to bring about a solution which will. 
redound to the interest not of any one particularly national 
group but to all national groups.
